currently ntfy server is setup behind authentik which forces google oauth. however, almost all ntfy clients do not support oauth features. the max they support are creating users with username and password to setup protected topics. I think we should revisit our ntfy auth. maybe we can setup access control for our topics
I'll help you set up proper access control for ntfy. Let me first understand the current ntfy configuration and explore options.

# ntfy server configuration
# https://docs.ntfy.sh/config/

# Listen address
listen-http: ":80"

# Base URL for links in notifications
base-url: "https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev"

# Cache settings
cache-file: "/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db"
cache-duration: "24h"

# Attachment settings
attachment-cache-dir: "/var/cache/ntfy/attachments"
attachment-total-size-limit: "1G"
attachment-file-size-limit: "50M"
attachment-expiry-duration: "24h"

# Rate limiting (relaxed for internal use)
visitor-request-limit-burst: 60
visitor-request-limit-replenish: "10s"

# Logging
log-level: "info"
log-format: "json"

# Metrics (for Prometheus scraping)
enable-metrics: true
metrics-listen-http: ":9090"

# Web UI
web-root: "/"
enable-web-push: true

# Custom templates
template-dir: "/etc/ntfy/templates"

# Upstream server (optional - for mobile push)
# upstream-base-url: "https://ntfy.sh"

# Authentication (optional - enable for access control)
# auth-file: "/var/lib/ntfy/user.db"
# auth-default-access: "deny-all"

1→services:
     2→  # ==========================================================================
     3→  # Loki - Log aggregation
     4→  # ==========================================================================
     5→  loki:
     6→    image: grafana/loki:3.5.9
     7→    container_name: loki
     8→    command: -config.file=/etc/loki/local-config.yaml
     9→    ports:
    10→      - "3100:3100"
    11→    volumes:
    12→      - ./loki/config.yaml:/etc/loki/local-config.yaml:ro
    13→      - loki_data:/loki
    14→    deploy:

    19→        reservations:
    20→          memory: 512m
    21→          cpus: '0.5'
    22→    restart: unless-stopped
    23→    healthcheck:
    24→      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3100/ready || exit 1"]
    25→      interval: 30s
    26→      timeout: 10s
    27→      retries: 3
    28→      start_period: 30s

    30→  # ==========================================================================

    32→  # ==========================================================================
    33→  alloy:
    34→    image: grafana/alloy:v1.12.1
    35→    container_name: alloy
    36→    command:
    37→      - run
    38→      - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
    39→      - --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data
    40→      - --disable-reporting=true
    41→      - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
    42→    ports:

    45→      - "12345:12345" # Alloy UI
    46→    volumes:
    47→      - ./alloy/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
    48→      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    49→      - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
    50→      - alloy_data:/var/lib/alloy/data
    51→    deploy:

    71→          exec 42<&-;
    72→          exec 42>&-'

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Loki - Log aggregation
  # ==========================================================================
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.5.9
    container_name: loki
    command: -config.file=/etc/loki/local-config.yaml
    ports:
      - "3100:3100"
    volumes:
      - ./loki/config.yaml:/etc/loki/local-config.yaml:ro
      - loki_data:/loki
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3100/ready || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana Alloy - Unified telemetry collector (replaces OTEL Collector)
  # ==========================================================================
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.12.1
    container_name: alloy
    command:
      - run
      - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
      - --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data
      - --disable-reporting=true
      - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver (backwards compat)
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver (backwards compat)
      - "12345:12345" # Alloy UI
    volumes:
      - ./alloy/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
      - alloy_data:/var/lib/alloy/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
      - loki
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - |
          bash -c '
          exec 42<>/dev/tcp/localhost/12345;
          echo -e "GET /-/healthy HTTP/1.1\nHost: localhost\nConnection: close\n\n" >&42;
          head -1 <&42 | cut -d" " -f2 | grep -q "^200$" || exit 1;
          exec 42<&-;
          exec 42>&-'
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.8.1
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
      - '--web.external-url=https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.30.0
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
      - '--web.external-url=https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:12.3.1
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_ENABLED=true
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_NAME=Authentik
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_SCOPES=openid email profile
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_AUTH_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_AUTH_URL}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_API_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_API_URL}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=true
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_AUTO_LOGIN=false
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_USE_PKCE=true
      - GF_AUTH_SIGNOUT_REDIRECT_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_SIGNOUT_URL}
      # Attribute mappings for user info from Authentik (using JMESPath)
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE_PATH=email
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_LOGIN_ATTRIBUTE_PATH=preferred_username || email
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_NAME_ATTRIBUTE_PATH=name || preferred_username
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2.0.2
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:2.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.15.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ./ntfy/templates:/etc/ntfy/templates:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  loki_data:
  alloy_data:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]

  # Pass env content to module - synced BEFORE docker compose runs
  env_content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = local.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = local.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = local.op.uptime_kuma_password
    discord_webhook_url    = local.op.discord_webhook_url
    # Grafana OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
    grafana_oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.grafana.client_id
    grafana_oauth_client_secret = random_password.grafana_oidc_secret.result
    grafana_oauth_auth_url      = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/authorize/"
    grafana_oauth_token_url     = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/token/"
    grafana_oauth_api_url       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/userinfo/"
    grafana_oauth_signout_url   = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/grafana/end-session/"
  })
}

# Note: .env file is now handled by the docker-lxc module via env_content
# This ensures the .env is synced BEFORE docker compose runs

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "grafana_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "grafana"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "grafana.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "prometheus_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prometheus"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9090"

  internal_domain = "prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "alertmanager_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "alertmanager"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9093"

  internal_domain = "alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "uptime_kuma_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "status"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3001"

  internal_domain = "status.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "ntfy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.monitoring.container_id
  container_ip   = module.monitoring.ip_address
  container_name = "monitoring"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-500"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,monitoring"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.monitoring.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.monitoring.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.monitoring.ssh_command
}

output "alloy_endpoints" {
  value = {
    grpc = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4317"
    http = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4318"
  }
}

output "loki_url" {
  value = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3100"
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.internal_url
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.internal_url
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.internal_url
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.internal_url
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.remote_config_path
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.remote_config_path
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.remote_config_path
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.remote_config_path
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

Here's what I found about ntfy access control and ACL topic permissions configuration:

## Overview

ntfy's auth is implemented with a simple SQLite-based backend. It implements two roles (user and admin) and per-topic read and write permissions using an access control list (ACL).(no content)Access control entries can be applied to users as well as the special everyone user (*), which represents anonymous API access.

## Configuration Setup

To set up auth, simply configure the following two options: `auth-file` is the user/access database; it is created automatically if it doesn't already exist; suggested location `/var/lib/ntfy/user.db`. `auth-default-access` defines the default/fallback access if no access control entry is found; it can be set to `read-write` (default), `read-only`, `write-only` or `deny-all`.(no content)The easiest way to configure a private instance is to set `auth-default-access` to `deny-all` in the server.yml.

## User Roles

Role user (default): Users with this role have no special permissions. Manage access using `ntfy access`.(no content)Role admin: Users with this role can read/write to all topics. Granular access control is not necessary.

## Managing Users (CLI Commands)

Example commands:
- `ntfy user list` - Shows list of users
- `ntfy user add phil` - Add regular user phil
- `ntfy user add --role=admin phil` - Add admin user phil
- `ntfy user del phil` - Delete user phil
- `ntfy user change-pass phil` - Change password for user phil
- `ntfy user change-role phil admin` - Make user phil an admin

## Access Control List (ACL) Commands

The ACL can be displayed or modified with the `ntfy access` command:
- `ntfy access` - Shows access control list
- `ntfy access USERNAME` - Shows access control entries for USERNAME  
- `ntfy access USERNAME TOPIC PERMISSION` - Allow/deny access for USERNAME to TOPIC

A USERNAME is an existing user, or the anonymous user `everyone` or `*`, which represents clients that access the API without username/password.

## Topic Patterns

A TOPIC is either a specific topic name (e.g. `mytopic`, or `phil_alerts`), or a wildcard pattern that matches any number of topics (e.g. `alerts_*` or `ben-*`). Only the wildcard character `*` is supported. It stands for zero to any number of characters.

## Permission Types

A PERMISSION is any of the following supported permissions:
- `read-write` (alias: rw): Allows publishing messages to the given topic, as well as subscribing and reading messages
- `read-only` (aliases: read, ro): Allows only subscribing and reading messages, but not publishing to the topic
- `write-only` (aliases: write, wo): Allows only publishing to the topic, but not subscribing to it
- `deny` (alias: none): Allows neither publishing nor subscribing to a topic

## Example ACL Configuration

In this example, phil has the role admin, so he has read-write access to all topics (no ACL entries are necessary). User ben has three topic-specific entries. He can read, but not write to topic furnace, and has read-write access to topic garagedoor and all topics starting with the word alerts (wildcards). Clients that are not authenticated (called */everyone) only have read access to the announcements and server-stats topics.

## Access Tokens

Access tokens provide an alternative authentication method that avoids storing passwords in client configurations. Tokens can have optional expiration dates, each user can have up to 20 tokens, and tokens provide the same level of access as the user account.

## Home Assistant Integration

The ntfy service was introduced in Home Assistant 2025.5, and it's used by 790 active installations.(no content)Depending on whether the server is configured to support access control, some topics may be read/write protected so that only users with the correct credentials can subscribe or publish to them. Based on my research, here's what I recommend for ntfy access control:

## Proposed Access Control Strategy

ntfy has built-in ACL that's perfect for your use case. Here's my recommendation:

### Access Model

| Topic Pattern | Anonymous | Authenticated User | Services (Alertmanager, PBS, etc.) |
|--------------|-----------|-------------------|-----------------------------------|
| `homelab-alerts` | ❌ deny | ✅ read | ✅ write-only |
| `backup-alerts` | ❌ deny | ✅ read | ✅ write-only |
| `*` (everything else) | ❌ deny | ✅ read-write | - |

### Users to Create

1. **Admin user** (`admin`) - Full access, for web UI management
2. **Personal user** (`darshan`) - Read-write access for subscribing on mobile/desktop
3. **Service account** (`alertmanager`) - Write-only to `homelab-alerts`
4. **Service account** (`pbs-backup`) - Write-only to `backup-alerts`

### Key Benefits

- Mobile apps work with username/password or access tokens
- Services publish with dedicated accounts (audit trail)
- Web UI accessible without OAuth
- Authentik middleware removed from Traefik route

# Alertmanager Configuration
# Routes alerts to ntfy for centralized notification aggregation

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# Route tree
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'severity']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: 'ntfy'

  routes:
    # Critical alerts - immediate notification with high priority
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'ntfy-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      repeat_interval: 1h

    # Warning alerts - batched notifications with default priority
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: 'ntfy'
      group_wait: 1m
      repeat_interval: 4h

# Inhibition rules
inhibit_rules:
  # Inhibit warning if critical is firing for same alertname
  - source_match:
      severity: 'critical'
    target_match:
      severity: 'warning'
    equal: ['alertname', 'instance']

# Receivers
receivers:
  # ntfy receiver for warnings
  - name: 'ntfy'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=alertmanager&priority=default&tags=warning,homelab'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          follow_redirects: true

  # ntfy receiver for critical alerts
  - name: 'ntfy-critical'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=alertmanager&priority=urgent&tags=rotating_light,critical'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          follow_redirects: true

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# PBS Backup Script for ${container_name} (Container ${container_id})
# =============================================================================
# Generated by lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module
# Namespace: ${namespace}
# Schedule: ${schedule}
# Retention: ${retention} backups
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

CONTAINER_ID="${container_id}"
NAMESPACE="${namespace}"
RETENTION="${retention}"
LOG_FILE="/var/log/pbs-backups/$${NAMESPACE}.log"

# PBS repository from environment (set by systemd service)
# PBS_REPOSITORY, PBS_NAMESPACE, PBS_PASSWORD, PBS_FINGERPRINT

# Backup paths
INCLUDE_PATHS=(
%{ for path in include_paths ~}
  "${path}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=(
%{ for pattern in exclude_paths ~}
  "${pattern}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"
NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS="${notify_on_success}"
NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE="${notify_on_failure}"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

# Legacy alert function (simple text) - kept for pre-backup hook failures
send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="$${3:-$${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Title: $${title}" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${message}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Send structured JSON notification using ntfy pbs-backup template
send_backup_notification() {
    local status="$1"
    local duration="$${2:-0}"
    local backup_size="$${3:-unknown}"
    local error_msg="$${4:-}"

    # Check if notification should be sent based on status
    if [ "$${status}" = "success" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Success notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Failure notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi

    # Escape error message for JSON (replace quotes and newlines)
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_msg=$(echo "$${error_msg}" | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | tr '\n' ' ')
    fi

    # Build JSON payload
    local error_field=""
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_field=",
  \"error_message\": \"$${error_msg}\""
    fi

    local json_payload="{
  \"status\": \"$${status}\",
  \"container_name\": \"${container_name}\",
  \"container_id\": \"${container_id}\",
  \"namespace\": \"$${NAMESPACE}\",
  \"duration\": $${duration},
  \"backup_size\": \"$${backup_size}\",
  \"retention\": $${RETENTION},
  \"timestamp\": \"$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')\"$${error_field}
}"

    # Set priority based on status
    local priority="$${NTFY_PRIORITY}"
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ]; then
        priority="high"
    fi

    log "Sending notification: status=$${status}, size=$${backup_size}, duration=$${duration}s"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${json_payload}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        local hook_exit_code=$?
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name} (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup and capture output for size parsing
    local backup_exit_code=0
    local backup_output=""
    backup_output=$(eval "$${backup_cmd}" 2>&1) || backup_exit_code=$?

    local end_time=$(date +%s)
    local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

    # Parse backup size from output (looks for "Uploaded: X.XX MiB" or "GiB")
    local backup_size="unknown"
    if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
        # Try to extract uploaded size from PBS output
        backup_size=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'Uploaded:\s*\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        if [ -z "$${backup_size}" ] || [ "$${backup_size}" = "unknown" ]; then
            # Fallback: try to get total size
            backup_size=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'total\s+\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        fi
    fi

    # Log the backup output
    echo "$${backup_output}" | while IFS= read -r line; do
        log "  $${line}"
    done

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s (size: $${backup_size})"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        # Send success notification
        send_backup_notification "success" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}"

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        # Capture error message (last few lines of output)
        local error_msg=""
        if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
            error_msg=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | tail -5)
        fi

        # Send failure notification
        send_backup_notification "failure" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}" "Exit code: $${backup_exit_code}. $${error_msg}"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

# Docker LXC Module

Opinionated module for deploying Docker-based applications in LXC containers on Proxmox.

## Features

- **All-in-one**: Combines lxc-base, file-sync, and remote-docker-compose-file
- **Docker-ready**: Uses pre-built Docker template for instant deployment
- **Declarative**: No manual provisioners or SSH connections
- **Flexible**: Supports privileged/unprivileged, custom resources, file permissions
- **Documented**: Automatic Proxmox notes generation

## Usage

```hcl
module "my_app" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  # Identity
  name         = "my-app"
  container_id = 150

  # Network
  ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"

  # Resources
  cores  = 2
  memory = 2048

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

  # SSH
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key

  # Proxmox notes
  service_description = "My application"
  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://my-app.homelab.rambtech.dev/"
  }
}
```

## Requirements

- Deploy directory must contain `docker-compose.yml`
- Docker-ready LXC template (default: debian-13-docker_1.0_amd64.tar.zst)
- SSH access to Proxmox host (for privileged container features)

## Directory Structure

```
tofu/apps/my-app/
├── main.tf              # Module usage
├── deploy/
│   ├── docker-compose.yml  # Required
│   ├── .env                # Optional
│   └── config/             # Optional additional configs
```

## Outputs

- `container_id` - Proxmox container ID
- `ip_address` - Container IP address
- `ssh_command` - SSH command string
- `mac_address` - Container MAC address
- `lxc_module` - The underlying lxc-base module

## Secret Management Pattern

For applications that need secrets in environment files:

```hcl
# 1. Create template file
# deploy/.env.tpl
DB_PASSWORD=${db_password}
API_KEY=${api_key}

# 2. Generate local file with secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "app_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    db_password = local.op.postgres_password
    api_key     = local.op.api_key
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/app.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

# 3. Sync to container
resource "filesync_file" "app_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.app_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = "192.168.1.150"
  mode        = "0600"
  depends_on  = [module.my_app]
}
```

**Benefits:**

- Fully declarative (no null_resource)
- Proper state tracking
- Secrets never in git
- Template-based configuration

## Common Patterns

### Privileged Containers

For applications binding to privileged ports (80, 443):

```hcl
module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"
  # ...
  unprivileged = false  # Required for ports < 1024
}
```

### File Permissions

For specific file permission requirements:

```hcl
module "my_app" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"
  # ...
  file_permissions = {
    "/config/scripts/backup.sh" = "0755"
    "/config/certs/cert.pem"    = "0400"
  }
}
```

### Custom Post-Sync Commands

Run additional commands after file sync:

```hcl
module "my_app" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"
  # ...
  post_sync_commands = [
    "chown -R 1000:1000 /config/data",
    "chmod +x /config/scripts/*.sh"
  ]
}
```

### Custom Notes

Add operational documentation to Proxmox UI:

```hcl
module "my_app" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"
  # ...
  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://my-app.homelab.rambtech.dev/"
    direct   = "http://192.168.1.150:8080"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Web UI", port = 8080, info = "Main application interface" },
    { name = "API", port = 3000, info = "REST API endpoint" }
  ]
}
```

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           docker-lxc Module                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                             │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │      lxc-base Module                 │  │
│  │  - Container creation                │  │
│  │  - Network configuration             │  │
│  │  - SSH key injection                 │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                    ▼                        │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │      file-sync Module                │  │
│  │  - Rsync deploy/ directory           │  │
│  │  - Set ownership/permissions         │  │
│  │  - Run post-sync commands            │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                    ▼                        │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  remote-docker-compose-file          │  │
│  │  - Validate docker-compose.yml       │  │
│  │  - Run docker compose up -d          │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                    ▼                        │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │      proxmox-notes Module            │  │
│  │  - Generate formatted notes          │  │
│  │  - Update container description      │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Troubleshooting

### Docker compose fails to start

```bash
# SSH to container
ssh root@192.168.1.150

# Check Docker status
systemctl status docker

# Check compose file syntax
cd /config && docker compose config

# View logs
cd /config && docker compose logs
```

### File sync issues

```bash
# Verify files were synced
ssh root@192.168.1.150 ls -la /config

# Check permissions
ssh root@192.168.1.150 stat /config/.env

# Manual rsync test
rsync -avz deploy/ root@192.168.1.150:/config/
```

### Container won't start

```bash
# Check Proxmox logs
ssh root@homelab pct status 150

# Check container config
ssh root@homelab pct config 150

# Start manually
ssh root@homelab pct start 150
```

## Examples

### Reference Implementations

- **[tofu/apps/traefik/](../../apps/traefik/)** - Privileged container with secret management
- **[tofu/apps/n8n/](../../apps/n8n/)** - Standard unprivileged deployment

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# ntfy User and ACL Setup Script
# =============================================================================
# Generated by OpenTofu - do not edit manually
# This script is idempotent - safe to run multiple times
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

CONTAINER_NAME="ntfy"

# Helper to run ntfy commands inside container
ntfy_cmd() {
    docker exec "$CONTAINER_NAME" ntfy "$@"
}

# Check if container is running
if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q "^$CONTAINER_NAME$"; then
    echo "Error: ntfy container is not running"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== ntfy User and ACL Setup ==="

# =============================================================================
# Create Users (idempotent - will fail silently if user exists)
# =============================================================================

echo "Setting up users..."

# Admin user
echo "${ntfy_admin_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add --role=admin "${ntfy_admin_user}" 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User '${ntfy_admin_user}' already exists"

# Personal user (darshan)
echo "${ntfy_darshan_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add darshan 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User 'darshan' already exists"

# Service accounts (write-only to specific topics)
echo "${ntfy_alertmanager_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add alertmanager 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User 'alertmanager' already exists"

echo "${ntfy_pbs_backup_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add pbs-backup 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User 'pbs-backup' already exists"

# =============================================================================
# Set up Access Control List (ACL)
# =============================================================================

echo "Setting up access control..."

# Personal user - full access to all topics
ntfy_cmd access darshan '*' rw 2>/dev/null || true

# Service accounts - write-only to specific topics
ntfy_cmd access alertmanager 'homelab-alerts' wo 2>/dev/null || true
ntfy_cmd access pbs-backup 'backup-alerts' wo 2>/dev/null || true

# Deny anonymous access (already default, but explicit)
ntfy_cmd access everyone '*' deny 2>/dev/null || true

# =============================================================================
# Display Current Configuration
# =============================================================================

echo ""
echo "=== Current Users ==="
ntfy_cmd user list

echo ""
echo "=== Current ACL ==="
ntfy_cmd access

echo ""
echo "=== Setup Complete ==="

  default = 500

variable "memory" {

  default = 4096

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)

  memory = var.memory

  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS="${notify_on_success}"
NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE="${notify_on_failure}"

# Helper Functions

log() {

%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    local backup_exit_code=0
    local backup_output=""
    backup_output=$(eval "$${backup_cmd}" 2>&1) || backup_exit_code=$?

            backup_size=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'total\s+\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        fi
    fi

    # Log the backup output
    echo "$${backup_output}" | while IFS= read -r line; do
        log "  $${line}"
    done

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s (size: $${backup_size})"

        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \

%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}

        cleanup_temp_files

        send_backup_notification "success" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}"

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else

        local error_msg=""
        if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
            error_msg=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | tail -5)
        fi

        # Send failure notification
        send_backup_notification "failure" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}" "Exit code: $${backup_exit_code}. $${error_msg}"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    fi

        exit 1
    fi

    exit 0

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# PBS Backup Script for ${container_name} (Container ${container_id})
# =============================================================================
# Generated by lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module
# Namespace: ${namespace}
# Schedule: ${schedule}
# Retention: ${retention} backups
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

CONTAINER_ID="${container_id}"
NAMESPACE="${namespace}"
RETENTION="${retention}"
LOG_FILE="/var/log/pbs-backups/$${NAMESPACE}.log"

# PBS repository from environment (set by systemd service)
# PBS_REPOSITORY, PBS_NAMESPACE, PBS_PASSWORD, PBS_FINGERPRINT

# Backup paths
INCLUDE_PATHS=(
%{ for path in include_paths ~}
  "${path}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=(
%{ for pattern in exclude_paths ~}
  "${pattern}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"
NTFY_USER="${ntfy_user}"
NTFY_PASSWORD="${ntfy_password}"
NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS="${notify_on_success}"
NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE="${notify_on_failure}"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

# Legacy alert function (simple text) - kept for pre-backup hook failures
send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="$${3:-$${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    local auth_args=()
    if [ -n "$${NTFY_USER}" ] && [ -n "$${NTFY_PASSWORD}" ]; then
        auth_args=(-u "$${NTFY_USER}:$${NTFY_PASSWORD}")
    fi

    curl -sf "$${auth_args[@]}" \
        -H "Title: $${title}" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${message}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Send structured JSON notification using ntfy pbs-backup template
send_backup_notification() {
    local status="$1"
    local duration="$${2:-0}"
    local backup_size="$${3:-unknown}"
    local error_msg="$${4:-}"

    # Check if notification should be sent based on status
    if [ "$${status}" = "success" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_SUCCESS}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Success notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ] && [ "$${NOTIFY_ON_FAILURE}" != "true" ]; then
        log "Failure notification disabled, skipping"
        return 0
    fi

    # Escape error message for JSON (replace quotes and newlines)
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_msg=$(echo "$${error_msg}" | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | tr '\n' ' ')
    fi

    # Build JSON payload
    local error_field=""
    if [ -n "$${error_msg}" ]; then
        error_field=",
  \"error_message\": \"$${error_msg}\""
    fi

    local json_payload="{
  \"status\": \"$${status}\",
  \"container_name\": \"${container_name}\",
  \"container_id\": \"${container_id}\",
  \"namespace\": \"$${NAMESPACE}\",
  \"duration\": $${duration},
  \"backup_size\": \"$${backup_size}\",
  \"retention\": $${RETENTION},
  \"timestamp\": \"$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')\"$${error_field}
}"

    # Set priority based on status
    local priority="$${NTFY_PRIORITY}"
    if [ "$${status}" = "failure" ]; then
        priority="high"
    fi

    log "Sending notification: status=$${status}, size=$${backup_size}, duration=$${duration}s"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${json_payload}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        local hook_exit_code=$?
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name} (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup and capture output for size parsing
    local backup_exit_code=0
    local backup_output=""
    backup_output=$(eval "$${backup_cmd}" 2>&1) || backup_exit_code=$?

    local end_time=$(date +%s)
    local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

    # Parse backup size from output (looks for "Uploaded: X.XX MiB" or "GiB")
    local backup_size="unknown"
    if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
        # Try to extract uploaded size from PBS output
        backup_size=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'Uploaded:\s*\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        if [ -z "$${backup_size}" ] || [ "$${backup_size}" = "unknown" ]; then
            # Fallback: try to get total size
            backup_size=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | grep -oP 'total\s+\K[0-9.]+\s*[GMK]iB' | tail -1 || echo "unknown")
        fi
    fi

    # Log the backup output
    echo "$${backup_output}" | while IFS= read -r line; do
        log "  $${line}"
    done

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s (size: $${backup_size})"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        # Send success notification
        send_backup_notification "success" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}"

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        # Capture error message (last few lines of output)
        local error_msg=""
        if [ -n "$${backup_output}" ]; then
            error_msg=$(echo "$${backup_output}" | tail -5)
        fi

        # Send failure notification
        send_backup_notification "failure" "$${duration}" "$${backup_size}" "Exit code: $${backup_exit_code}. $${error_msg}"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

# Alertmanager Configuration
# Routes alerts to ntfy for centralized notification aggregation

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# Route tree
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'severity']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: 'ntfy'

  routes:
    # Critical alerts - immediate notification with high priority
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'ntfy-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      repeat_interval: 1h

    # Warning alerts - batched notifications with default priority
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: 'ntfy'
      group_wait: 1m
      repeat_interval: 4h

# Inhibition rules
inhibit_rules:
  # Inhibit warning if critical is firing for same alertname
  - source_match:
      severity: 'critical'
    target_match:
      severity: 'warning'
    equal: ['alertname', 'instance']

# Receivers
receivers:
  # ntfy receiver for warnings
  - name: 'ntfy'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=alertmanager&priority=default&tags=warning,homelab'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          follow_redirects: true

  # ntfy receiver for critical alerts

    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=alertmanager&priority=urgent&tags=rotating_light,critical'

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Loki - Log aggregation
  # ==========================================================================
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.5.9
    container_name: loki
    command: -config.file=/etc/loki/local-config.yaml
    ports:
      - "3100:3100"
    volumes:
      - ./loki/config.yaml:/etc/loki/local-config.yaml:ro
      - loki_data:/loki
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3100/ready || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana Alloy - Unified telemetry collector (replaces OTEL Collector)
  # ==========================================================================
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.12.1
    container_name: alloy
    command:
      - run
      - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
      - --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data
      - --disable-reporting=true
      - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver (backwards compat)
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver (backwards compat)
      - "12345:12345" # Alloy UI
    volumes:
      - ./alloy/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
      - alloy_data:/var/lib/alloy/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
      - loki
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - |
          bash -c '
          exec 42<>/dev/tcp/localhost/12345;
          echo -e "GET /-/healthy HTTP/1.1\nHost: localhost\nConnection: close\n\n" >&42;
          head -1 <&42 | cut -d" " -f2 | grep -q "^200$" || exit 1;
          exec 42<&-;
          exec 42>&-'
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.8.1
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
      - '--web.external-url=https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.30.0
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
      - '--web.external-url=https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:12.3.1
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_ENABLED=true
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_NAME=Authentik
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_SCOPES=openid email profile
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_AUTH_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_AUTH_URL}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_API_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_API_URL}
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=true
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_AUTO_LOGIN=false
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_USE_PKCE=true
      - GF_AUTH_SIGNOUT_REDIRECT_URL=${GRAFANA_OAUTH_SIGNOUT_URL}
      # Attribute mappings for user info from Authentik (using JMESPath)
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE_PATH=email
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_LOGIN_ATTRIBUTE_PATH=preferred_username || email
      - GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_NAME_ATTRIBUTE_PATH=name || preferred_username
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2.0.2
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:2.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.15.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ./ntfy/templates:/etc/ntfy/templates:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  loki_data:
  alloy_data:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:

      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2.0.2
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:2.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.15.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ./ntfy/templates:/etc/ntfy/templates:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  alloy_data:
  prometheus_data:
