#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# ntfy User and ACL Setup Script
# =============================================================================
# Generated by OpenTofu - do not edit manually
# This script is idempotent - safe to run multiple times
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

CONTAINER_NAME="ntfy"

# Helper to run ntfy commands inside container
ntfy_cmd() {
    docker exec "$CONTAINER_NAME" ntfy "$@"
}

# Check if container is running
if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q "^$CONTAINER_NAME$"; then
    echo "Error: ntfy container is not running"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== ntfy User and ACL Setup ==="

# =============================================================================
# Create Users (idempotent - will fail silently if user exists)
# =============================================================================

echo "Setting up users..."

# Admin user
echo "${ntfy_admin_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add --role=admin "${ntfy_admin_user}" 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User '${ntfy_admin_user}' already exists"

# Personal user (darshan)
echo "${ntfy_darshan_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add darshan 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User 'darshan' already exists"

# Service accounts (write-only to specific topics)
echo "${ntfy_alertmanager_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add alertmanager 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User 'alertmanager' already exists"

echo "${ntfy_pbs_backup_password}" | ntfy_cmd user add pbs-backup 2>/dev/null || \
    echo "  User 'pbs-backup' already exists"

# =============================================================================
# Set up Access Control List (ACL)
# =============================================================================

echo "Setting up access control..."

# Personal user - full access to all topics
ntfy_cmd access darshan '*' rw 2>/dev/null || true

# Service accounts - write-only to specific topics
ntfy_cmd access alertmanager 'homelab-alerts' wo 2>/dev/null || true
ntfy_cmd access pbs-backup 'backup-alerts' wo 2>/dev/null || true

# Deny anonymous access (already default, but explicit)
ntfy_cmd access everyone '*' deny 2>/dev/null || true

# =============================================================================
# Display Current Configuration
# =============================================================================

echo ""
echo "=== Current Users ==="
ntfy_cmd user list

echo ""
echo "=== Current ACL ==="
ntfy_cmd access

echo ""
echo "=== Setup Complete ==="

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]

  # Pass env content to module - synced BEFORE docker compose runs
  env_content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = local.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = local.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = local.op.uptime_kuma_password

    grafana_oauth_signout_url   = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/grafana/end-session/"

  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \

# View Alloy logs

ssh root@10.100.5.100 /config/ntfy/setup-users.sh

# =============================================================================
# n8n LXC - Workflow Automation
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 502
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Plus traefik-route module for self-service routing.
# =============================================================================

module "n8n" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  # Identity
  name         = "n8n"
  container_id = 502

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores          = 2
  memory         = 2048
  swap           = 1024
  rootfs_size    = 8
  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

      failed_when: false
      changed_when: "'user' in user_result.stdout or user_result.rc == 0"

      loop_control:

      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: >
          docker exec {{ ntfy_container }} ntfy access
          "{{ item.user }}" "{{ item.topic }}" "{{ item.permission }}"
      loop: "{{ access_rules }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.user }} -> {{ item.topic }}: {{ item.permission }}"
      register: acl_result

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:

#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for external access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.traefik}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module), env templates, and .tpl files
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env", "\\.tpl$"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.traefik_ip}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

  value = module.traefik.container_id

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.traefik.ip_address

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]

  # Pass env content to module - synced BEFORE docker compose runs
  env_content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = local.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = local.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = local.op.uptime_kuma_password
    discord_webhook_url    = local.op.discord_webhook_url
    # Grafana OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
    grafana_oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.grafana.client_id
    grafana_oauth_client_secret = random_password.grafana_oidc_secret.result
    grafana_oauth_auth_url      = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/authorize/"
    grafana_oauth_token_url     = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/token/"
    grafana_oauth_api_url       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/userinfo/"
    grafana_oauth_signout_url   = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/grafana/end-session/"
    # ntfy credentials for Alertmanager
    ntfy_alertmanager_password = local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password
  })
}

# Note: .env file is now handled by the docker-lxc module via env_content
# This ensures the .env is synced BEFORE docker compose runs

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ntfy User Provisioning (Ansible)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provisions ntfy users and ACL after container deployment

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "ntfy_provision" {
  triggers = {
    container_id = module.monitoring.container_id
    container_ip = module.monitoring.ip_address
    # Re-run if credentials change
    credentials_hash = sha256(join(",", [
      local.op.ntfy_admin_password,
      local.op.ntfy_darshan_password,
      local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password,
      local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password,
      local.op.ntfy_n8n_password,
    ]))
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/ntfy/provision-users.yml.tpl", {
    ntfy_admin_user            = local.op.ntfy_admin_user
    ntfy_admin_password        = local.op.ntfy_admin_password
    ntfy_darshan_password      = local.op.ntfy_darshan_password
    ntfy_alertmanager_password = local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password
    ntfy_pbs_backup_password   = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
    ntfy_n8n_password          = local.op.ntfy_n8n_password
  })

  inventory = yamlencode({
    monitoring = {
      hosts = {
        "monitoring" = {
          ansible_host = module.monitoring.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "grafana_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "grafana"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "grafana.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "prometheus_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prometheus"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9090"

  internal_domain = "prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "alertmanager_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "alertmanager"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9093"

  internal_domain = "alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "uptime_kuma_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "status"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3001"

  internal_domain = "status.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "ntfy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # ntfy has its own ACL-based authentication - no Authentik middleware
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.monitoring.container_id
  container_ip   = module.monitoring.ip_address
  container_name = "monitoring"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00"  # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-500"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,monitoring"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.monitoring.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.monitoring.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.monitoring.ssh_command
}

output "alloy_endpoints" {
  value = {
    grpc = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4317"
    http = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4318"
  }
}

output "loki_url" {
  value = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3100"
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.internal_url
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.internal_url
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.internal_url
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.internal_url
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.remote_config_path
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.remote_config_path
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.remote_config_path
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.remote_config_path
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Container Management LXC - Pulse + Arcane
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 104
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Container monitoring (Pulse) and management (Arcane).
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 104
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 16
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Container Management LXC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "container_mgmt" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "container-mgmt"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only - no LAN access needed)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.core.container_mgmt}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 512

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude runtime data directories from sync (they're managed by the apps)
  exclude_patterns = ["pulse/**", "arcane_data/**"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Container Management"
  service_description = "Pulse monitoring + Arcane container management"

  service_urls = {
    pulse  = "https://pulse.${var.domain_internal}"
    arcane = "https://arcane.${var.domain_internal}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Pulse", port = 7655, info = "Proxmox + Docker monitoring" },
    { name = "Arcane", port = 3552, info = "Docker container management" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Pulse - Container Monitoring

Real-time monitoring for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
- Dashboard: https://pulse.${var.domain_internal}
- Proxmox metrics via PVE API
- Docker metrics via socket

## Arcane - Container Management

Docker container management with update detection.
- Dashboard: https://arcane.${var.domain_internal}
- Remote agents connect from other LXCs

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f pulse
cd /config && docker compose logs -f arcane
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=container-mgmt` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["pulse", "arcane", "management"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "local_sensitive_file" "container_mgmt_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    pulse_admin_user      = local.op.pulse_admin_user
    pulse_admin_password  = local.op.pulse_admin_password
    arcane_encryption_key = local.op.arcane_encryption_key
    arcane_jwt_secret     = local.op.arcane_jwt_secret
    # Pulse OIDC
    pulse_oidc_issuer        = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/pulse/"
    pulse_oidc_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.pulse.client_id
    pulse_oidc_client_secret = random_password.pulse_oidc_secret.result
    # Arcane OIDC
    arcane_oidc_issuer        = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/arcane/"
    arcane_oidc_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.arcane.client_id
    arcane_oidc_client_secret = random_password.arcane_oidc_secret.result
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/container-mgmt.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "container_mgmt_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.container_mgmt_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.container_mgmt.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "pulse_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "pulse"
  backend_url = "http://${module.container_mgmt.ip_address}:7655"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "pulse.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Pulse uses native OIDC - no forward auth needed
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

module "arcane_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "arcane"
  backend_url = "http://${module.container_mgmt.ip_address}:3552"

  internal_domain = "arcane.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Arcane uses its own auth - native OIDC doesn't persist reliably
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "container_mgmt_sidecars" {

  container_id   = module.container_mgmt.container_id
  container_ip   = module.container_mgmt.ip_address

    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00" # Weekly backup

    namespace = "lxc-104"

    pre_backup_commands = [] # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"

  }

    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {

    arcane = module.arcane_route.internal_url
  }
}

  value = {
    pulse  = module.pulse_route.remote_config_path
    arcane = module.arcane_route.remote_config_path
  }

The granular access control happens via ACL entries, not roles. ntfy's design is that you set `auth-default-access: deny-all` and then explicitly grant permissions per user/topic combination.

# =============================================================================
# Authentik LXC - Identity Provider (SSO/OIDC)
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 203
#
# Replaces Authelia with a more feature-rich identity provider:
#   - Native Google/GitHub OAuth federation
#   - OIDC provider for apps with native SSO support
#   - Forward auth for apps without native OAuth
#   - Centralized user/group management
#
# File Structure:
#   - main.tf:      Container, env, routes, sidecars
#   - providers.tf: OAuth sources, forward auth, OIDC providers
#   - users.tf:     User management (SOPS-encrypted)
#   - outputs.tf:   All outputs
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Authentik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 203
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 4096  # Authentik recommended minimum
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 16
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "authentik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "authentik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only - Traefik handles external access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.authentik}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude .env template files (we generate .env from template)
  exclude_patterns = ["^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Authentik"
  service_description = "Identity Provider - SSO, OIDC, and forward auth for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {

# =============================================================================
# OpenWebUI LXC - AI Chat Interface with llama.cpp
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 501
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Features Vulkan GPU acceleration for llama.cpp (AMD Radeon 890M gfx1150).
#
# Benchmarked performance (Vulkan vs ROCm vs CPU):
#   - Vulkan: ~800 tok/s prompt, ~40 tok/s generation (WINNER)
#   - ROCm:   ~30 tok/s prompt,  ~29 tok/s generation
#   - CPU:    ~28 tok/s prompt,  ~28 tok/s generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Mount points - LLM models on ZFS tank for unlimited storage
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/llm-models"
      volume = "/tank/llm-models"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Make download script executable
  file_permissions = {
    "/config/download-model.sh" = "0755"
  }

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with llama.cpp backend (Vulkan GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "llama-server", port = 8080, info = "LLM backend (Vulkan GPU)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) via Vulkan/RADV:
- `/dev/dri` device passthrough
- ~40 tok/s generation, ~800 tok/s prompt processing

**Check GPU detection:**
```
docker logs llama-server 2>&1 | grep -i vulkan
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f llama-server
```

**Test inference:**
```
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3.2-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```

**Download new model (GGUF format):**
```
cd /llm-models
curl -L -O "https://huggingface.co/bartowski/MODEL/resolve/main/MODEL.gguf"
```

Models are stored on ZFS tank (`/tank/llm-models` → `/llm-models`).

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "llama-cpp", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "openwebui_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    webui_secret_key    = random_password.openwebui_secret_key.result
    oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.openwebui.client_id
    oauth_client_secret = random_password.openwebui_oidc_secret.result
    openid_provider_url = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/openwebui/.well-known/openid-configuration"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/openwebui.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "openwebui_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.openwebui_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.openwebui.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.openwebui.container_id
  container_ip   = module.openwebui.ip_address
  container_name = "openwebui"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-501"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database dump needed - SQLite file backup is sufficient

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]  # Models are on /tank, not backed up here

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,openwebui"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenWebUI (AI Chat Interface)
module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal and public routes (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "ai.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# llama.cpp API (LLM Backend - OpenAI compatible)
module "llama_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "llama"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal only (OpenAI-compatible API access)
  internal_domain = "llama.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Basic auth for API access
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "llama-auth"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    openwebui = {
      internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
      public   = module.openwebui_route.public_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
    }
    llama = {
      internal = module.llama_route.internal_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"
    }
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    openwebui = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
    llama     = module.llama_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Network Services LXC - AdGuard + Cloudflared + DDNS
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 101
#
# Core network infrastructure: DNS (AdGuard Home), Cloudflare tunnel, DDNS.
# Tailscale runs as systemd service (requires kernel access).
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 101
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "cloudflare_ddns_domains" {
  type    = string
  default = "homelab.rambtech.dev"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Network Services Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "network_services" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "network-services"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for DNS service)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.core.network_services}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.network_services}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for Tailscale kernel access
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude AdGuard config - managed separately via templating for dns_mode toggle
  exclude_patterns = ["AdGuardHome\\.yaml$", "\\.tpl$"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Network Services"
  service_description = "Core network infrastructure: DNS, tunnels, and VPN"

  service_urls = {
    adguard_internal = "https://dns.${var.domain_internal}"
    adguard_direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.network_services}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "AdGuard Home", port = 53, info = "DNS server with ad blocking" },
    { name = "AdGuard UI", port = 3000, info = "Web management interface" },
    { name = "Cloudflared", port = 0, info = "Cloudflare tunnel (outbound only)" },
    { name = "Tailscale", port = 41641, info = "Mesh VPN (systemd service)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Tailscale Management

Tailscale runs as a systemd service (not Docker) because it requires kernel-level network access.

**Check status:**
```bash
systemctl status tailscaled
tailscale status
```

**Restart if needed:**
```bash
systemctl restart tailscaled
```

## Docker Services

**View logs:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose logs -f <service>
```

**Restart all services:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose restart
```

## DNS Testing

**Test AdGuard (port 53):**
```bash
dig @${local.lan_ips.network_services} google.com
```

**Test internal DNS rewrites:**
```bash
dig @${local.lan_ips.network_services} traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=network-services` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["network-services", "dns", "adguard", "cloudflare"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "network_services_env" {
  content = <<-EOT
# Network Services Environment Variables
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Cloudflare Tunnel Token
CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=${local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token}

# Cloudflare API Token for DDNS
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=${local.op.cloudflare_api_token}

# Domains to update with DDNS
CLOUDFLARE_DDNS_DOMAINS=${var.cloudflare_ddns_domains}
EOT

  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/network-services.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "network_services_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.network_services_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.network_services.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.network_services]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AdGuard Home Configuration (DNS Mode Toggle)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generates AdGuard config based on dns_mode variable:
# - home: Uses LAN IPs (192.168.1.x) - works on home network without Tailscale
# - travel: Uses container IPs (10.100.x.x) - routes through Tailscale, avoids subnet conflicts

locals {
  # Select IP based on dns_mode
  adguard_traefik_ip = var.dns_mode == "travel" ? local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik : local.lan_ips.traefik
}

resource "local_file" "adguard_config" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/adguard/conf/AdGuardHome.yaml.tpl", {
    dns_mode   = var.dns_mode
    traefik_ip = local.adguard_traefik_ip
  })

  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/AdGuardHome.yaml"
  file_permission = "0644"
}

resource "filesync_file" "adguard_config" {
  source      = local_file.adguard_config.filename
  destination = "/config/adguard/conf/AdGuardHome.yaml"
  host        = module.network_services.ip_address

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.network_services]
}

# Restart AdGuard when config changes
resource "null_resource" "restart_adguard" {
  triggers = {
    config_hash = local_file.adguard_config.content_md5
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "docker restart adguard || true"
    ]

    connection {
      type        = "ssh"
      user        = "root"
      host        = module.network_services.ip_address
      private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }
  }

  depends_on = [filesync_file.adguard_config]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tailscale Service Management via Ansible
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensures Tailscale daemon is running and connected after deployment

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "manage_tailscale" {
  depends_on = [module.network_services]

  # Re-run when container is rebuilt or network config changes
  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
    lan_ip       = local.lan_ips.network_services
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false  # Run ansible directly on host
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = <<-EOT
    - name: Manage Tailscale service on network-services
      hosts: lxc
      gather_facts: no
      vars:
        app_name: network-services

      tasks:
        # =====================================================================
        # Tailscale Service Management
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Ensure Tailscale daemon is running
          ansible.builtin.systemd:
            name: tailscaled
            state: started
            enabled: true
          register: tailscale_service

        - name: Wait for Tailscale to initialize
          ansible.builtin.pause:
            seconds: 3
          when: tailscale_service.changed

        # =====================================================================
        # Verify Tailscale Status
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Check Tailscale connection status
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: tailscale status --json
          register: tailscale_status
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: false

        - name: Parse Tailscale status
          ansible.builtin.set_fact:
            tailscale_info: "{{ tailscale_status.stdout | from_json }}"
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Display Tailscale connection info
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: |
              Tailscale Status: {{ 'Connected' if (tailscale_info.BackendState | default('')) == 'Running' else 'Not Connected' }}
              Tailnet IP: {{ tailscale_info.Self.TailscaleIPs[0] | default('N/A') }}
              Hostname: {{ tailscale_info.Self.HostName | default('N/A') }}
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Warn if Tailscale not connected
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: "WARNING: Tailscale is not connected. Check authentication status with 'tailscale status'"
          when: tailscale_status.rc != 0 or (tailscale_info.BackendState | default('')) != 'Running'
  EOT

  inventory = yamlencode({
    lxc = {
      hosts = {
        "network-services" = {
          ansible_host = module.network_services.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}

---
# =============================================================================
# ntfy User Provisioning Playbook
# =============================================================================
# This playbook sets up ntfy users and access control.
# Generated by OpenTofu - do not edit manually.
# =============================================================================

- name: Provision ntfy users and ACL
  hosts: monitoring
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    ntfy_container: ntfy
    users:
      - name: "${ntfy_admin_user}"
        password: "${ntfy_admin_password}"
        role: admin
      - name: darshan
        password: "${ntfy_darshan_password}"
        role: user
      - name: alertmanager
        password: "${ntfy_alertmanager_password}"
        role: user
      - name: pbs-backup
        password: "${ntfy_pbs_backup_password}"
        role: user
      - name: n8n
        password: "${ntfy_n8n_password}"
        role: user
    access_rules:
      - user: darshan
        topic: "*"
        permission: rw
      - user: alertmanager
        topic: "homelab-alerts"
        permission: wo
      - user: pbs-backup
        topic: "backup-alerts"
        permission: wo
      - user: n8n
        topic: "*"
        permission: rw
      - user: everyone
        topic: "*"
        permission: deny

  tasks:
    - name: Wait for ntfy container to be running
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker inspect -f '{{ "{{" }}.State.Running{{ "}}" }}' {{ ntfy_container }}
      register: container_check
      until: container_check.stdout == "true"
      retries: 30
      delay: 2
      changed_when: false

    - name: Create ntfy users
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        echo "{{ item.password }}" | docker exec -i {{ ntfy_container }} ntfy user add \
          {% if item.role == 'admin' %}--role=admin{% endif %} \
          "{{ item.name }}"
      loop: "{{ users }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.name }}"
      register: user_result
      failed_when: false
      changed_when: "'user' in user_result.stdout or user_result.rc == 0"

    - name: Report user creation results
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "User '{{ item.item.name }}': {{ 'created' if item.rc == 0 else 'already exists or failed' }}"
      loop: "{{ user_result.results }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.item.name }}"

    - name: Set access control rules
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: >
          docker exec {{ ntfy_container }} ntfy access
          "{{ item.user }}" "{{ item.topic }}" "{{ item.permission }}"
      loop: "{{ access_rules }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.user }} -> {{ item.topic }}: {{ item.permission }}"
      register: acl_result
      failed_when: false
      changed_when: acl_result.rc == 0

    - name: Display current users
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker exec {{ ntfy_container }} ntfy user list
      register: users_list
      changed_when: false

    - name: Display current ACL
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker exec {{ ntfy_container }} ntfy access
      register: acl_list
      changed_when: false

    - name: Show final configuration
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== ntfy Users ==="
          - "{{ users_list.stdout_lines }}"
          - "=== ntfy ACL ==="
          - "{{ acl_list.stdout_lines }}"

content.text: Fixed. Now `darshan` has read-only (`ro`) access - can subscribe to all topics but cannot publish.
and what if we want to give say alertmanager write access to multiple topics? would we just create another rule?

Yes, exactly. You'd add another rule for the same user with a different topic. Let me show you how that would look:

```yaml
access_rules:
  - user: alertmanager
    topic: "homelab-alerts"
    permission: wo
  - user: alertmanager
    topic: "critical-alerts"
    permission: wo
  - user: alertmanager
    topic: "warnings"
    permission: wo
```

Or you could use a wildcard pattern if the topics share a prefix:

```yaml
access_rules:
  - user: alertmanager
    topic: "alerts-*"      # Matches alerts-critical, alerts-warning, etc.
    permission: wo
```

ntfy supports the `*` wildcard which matches zero or more characters. So you could structure your topics as:
- `alerts-homelab`
- `alerts-backup`
- `alerts-critical`

And give alertmanager access with a single rule: `topic: "alerts-*"`

I notice that admin isnt explicitly given any access to topics. is that by design? will admin user still be able publish/subscribe to all topics and manager users?

Yes, that's by design. In ntfy, the `admin` role automatically grants full access to everything:

- **Read/write access to all topics** - no ACL entries needed
- **User management** - can add/remove users, change passwords
- **ACL management** - can modify access control rules

From the [ntfy docs](https://ntfy.sh/docs/config/): "Users with the admin role can read/write to all topics. Granular access control is not necessary."

So the admin user doesn't need any explicit ACL entries - the role itself provides unrestricted access. The ACL rules only apply to regular `user` role accounts.
oohh theres also: https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy-ansible

Nice find! That's an official Ansible collection for ntfy. However, looking at the repo, it's designed for installing and configuring the ntfy server itself, not for managing users/ACL on an already-running Docker container.

The collection's roles are:
- `ntfy.ntfy.install` - Install ntfy server
- `ntfy.ntfy.configure` - Configure server settings

For our use case (provisioning users via `docker exec` on an existing container), the simple playbook I created is actually more appropriate. The official collection would be useful if we were installing ntfy directly on a host instead of running it in Docker.

That said, if you want to use access tokens instead of passwords for mobile clients, ntfy supports that too. You could generate tokens for the `darshan` user which is more secure than storing the password in the mobile app. Want me to add token generation to the provisioning playbook?

This is AutoKuma's monitor definitions, not the notification config. Uptime Kuma's notification settings are configured in the UI and stored in its database volume, not in these declarative configs.

You'll need to update the ntfy notification settings in Uptime Kuma's UI after deployment:

1. Go to **Settings → Notifications** in Uptime Kuma
2. Edit the ntfy notification 
3. Add authentication (username: `alertmanager`, password from 1Password)

Alternatively, we could create a new service account specifically for Uptime Kuma. Do you want to:

1. **Reuse `alertmanager` account** - Both Alertmanager and Uptime Kuma share credentials (simpler)
2. **Create `uptime-kuma` account** - Separate service account with its own ACL (more granular auditing)

For now, let's proceed with deployment. The Uptime Kuma notification can be updated manually in the UI after, since AutoKuma doesn't manage notification configs.

Ready to deploy?

```bash
task tofu:init APP=monitoring
task tofu:plan APP=monitoring
```
can we do it declaratively though? using autokuma?
Let me check the AutoKuma documentation to see if it supports notification configuration.

Based on my search results, here's what I found about AutoKuma and declarative configuration for Uptime Kuma notifications:

## AutoKuma Overview

AutoKuma is a utility that automates the creation of Uptime Kuma monitors based on Docker container labels. With AutoKuma, you can eliminate the need for manual monitor creation in the Uptime Kuma UI.(no content)Kuma CLI is a Command Line Interface (CLI) tool for managing and interacting with Uptime Kuma. With Kuma CLI you can easily configure, monitor and manage your applications from the command line.

## Declarative Configuration

AutoKuma allows us to set labels on our Docker containers that will then automatically generate monitors in UptimeKuma. For example, containers can have labels like:
```
labels:
  kuma.monitoring.group.name: "Monitoring"
  kuma.uptime_kuma.http.parent_name: "monitoring"
  kuma.uptime_kuma.http.name: "Kuma status monitoring"
  kuma.uptime_kuma.http.url: "http://${HOST_IP}:3001"
```(no content)AutoKuma will read configuration from a file named autokuma.{toml,yaml,json}. Labels are grouped by id into a single monitor. For example, to create a simple HTTP monitor, use labels like:
```yaml
kuma.example.http.name: "Example"
kuma.example.http.url: "https://example.com"
```

## Notifications Configuration

To assign a monitor to a group, set its parent_name property to the autokuma id of the group. However, "Defining Notifications is currently experimental and might change in the future."

## Docker Compose Example

AutoKuma can be deployed via Docker Compose with environment variables like:
- `AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL`
- `AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME`
- `AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD`
- `AUTOKUMA__TAG_NAME`
- `AUTOKUMA__DEFAULT_SETTINGS`(no content)Uptime Kuma itself supports notifications via Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, Email (SMTP), and 90+ notification services.

Note that while AutoKuma provides declarative configuration for monitors, the notifications feature is still marked as experimental according to the documentation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent:
The user wants to set up proper access control for ntfy push notification server. Currently ntfy is behind Authentik OAuth, but ntfy mobile/desktop clients don't support OAuth - they only support username/password authentication. The goal is to:
- Remove Authentik middleware from ntfy route
- Enable ntfy's native ACL-based authentication
- Create service accounts for: admin, personal user (darshan), alertmanager, pbs-backup, n8n
- Configure topic-based permissions for each user
- Update all services (Alertmanager, PBS backups) to authenticate with ntfy

## 2. Key Technical Concepts:
- **ntfy ACL system**: Two roles (admin/user), per-topic permissions (ro/wo/rw/deny)
- **ntfy CLI commands**: `ntfy user add`, `ntfy access`, `ntfy user list`
- **1Password integration**: Data sources with section-based field extraction
- **Ansible provisioning**: Using `ansible_navigator_run` resource in OpenTofu
- **Docker secrets**: For Alertmanager password file
- **Traefik middleware**: Removing Authentik for ntfy native auth
- **lxc-sidecars module**: PBS backup scripts with ntfy authentication
- **AutoKuma**: Declarative Uptime Kuma monitor configuration (notifications experimental)

## 3. Files and Code Sections:

### `tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ntfy/server.yml`
- Enabled authentication by uncommenting auth settings
```yaml
# Authentication - Enable access control with ACL
auth-file: "/var/lib/ntfy/user.db"
auth-default-access: "deny-all"
```

### `tofu/onepassword.tf`
- Added ntfy data source and credential extraction
```hcl
data "onepassword_item" "ntfy" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "ntfy"
}

# Flatten ntfy section fields by section name
_ntfy_users_fields = merge([
  for s in try(data.onepassword_item.ntfy.section, []) : s.label == "users" ? {
    for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
  } : {}
]...)

_ntfy_services_fields = merge([
  for s in try(data.onepassword_item.ntfy.section, []) : s.label == "services" ? {
    for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
  } : {}
]...)

# In local.op:
ntfy_admin_user              = data.onepassword_item.ntfy.username
ntfy_admin_password          = data.onepassword_item.ntfy.password
ntfy_darshan_password        = lookup(local._ntfy_users_fields, "darshan_password", "")
ntfy_alertmanager_password   = lookup(local._ntfy_services_fields, "alertmanager_password", "")
ntfy_pbs_backup_password     = lookup(local._ntfy_services_fields, "pbs_backup_password", "")
ntfy_n8n_password            = lookup(local._ntfy_services_fields, "n8n_password", "")
```

### `tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ntfy/provision-users.yml.tpl` (NEW)
- Ansible playbook for ntfy user/ACL provisioning
```yaml
---
- name: Provision ntfy users and ACL
  hosts: monitoring
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    ntfy_container: ntfy
    users:
      - name: "${ntfy_admin_user}"
        password: "${ntfy_admin_password}"
        role: admin
      - name: darshan
        password: "${ntfy_darshan_password}"
        role: user
      - name: alertmanager
        password: "${ntfy_alertmanager_password}"
        role: user
      - name: pbs-backup
        password: "${ntfy_pbs_backup_password}"
        role: user
      - name: n8n
        password: "${ntfy_n8n_password}"
        role: user
    access_rules:
      - user: darshan
        topic: "*"
        permission: ro  # Subscribe only - no publishing needed
      - user: alertmanager
        topic: "homelab-alerts"
        permission: wo
      - user: pbs-backup
        topic: "backup-alerts"
        permission: wo
      - user: n8n
        topic: "docker-updates"
        permission: rw
      - user: everyone
        topic: "*"
        permission: deny
  # ... tasks to create users and set ACL via docker exec
```

### `tofu/apps/monitoring/main.tf`
- Added Ansible provisioning resource and removed Authentik from ntfy route
```hcl
resource "ansible_navigator_run" "ntfy_provision" {
  triggers = {
    container_id = module.monitoring.container_id
    container_ip = module.monitoring.ip_address
    credentials_hash = sha256(join(",", [
      local.op.ntfy_admin_password,
      local.op.ntfy_darshan_password,
      local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password,
      local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password,
      local.op.ntfy_n8n_password,
    ]))
  }
  # ... ansible config with templated playbook
  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  # ...
  # ntfy has its own ACL-based authentication - no Authentik middleware
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]  # Removed "authentik"
}
```

### `tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml`
- Added basic_auth to ntfy webhook receivers
```yaml
receivers:
  - name: 'ntfy'
    webhook_configs:
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=alertmanager&priority=default&tags=warning,homelab'

            username: alertmanager
            password_file: /run/secrets/ntfy_password
```

### `tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/docker-compose.yml`
- Added secrets section for alertmanager
```yaml
  alertmanager:
    # ...
    secrets:
      - ntfy_password

secrets:
  ntfy_password:
    environment: NTFY_ALERTMANAGER_PASSWORD
```

### `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/variables.tf`
- Added ntfy_user and ntfy_password to backup config
```hcl
ntfy_user          = optional(string, "")   # ntfy username for authentication
ntfy_password      = optional(string, "")   # ntfy password for authentication
```

### `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl`
- Added authentication to curl commands
```bash
NTFY_USER="${ntfy_user}"
NTFY_PASSWORD="${ntfy_password}"

send_alert() {
    local auth_args=()
    if [ -n "${NTFY_USER}" ] && [ -n "${NTFY_PASSWORD}" ]; then
        auth_args=(-u "${NTFY_USER}:${NTFY_PASSWORD}")
    fi
    curl -sf "${auth_args[@]}" ...
}
```

### All 12 app backup configs updated
- n8n, traefik, immich, documents, monitoring, media-management, container-mgmt, authentik, dashboards, jellyfin, openwebui, network-services
```hcl
backup = {
  # ...
  ntfy_user     = "pbs-backup"
  ntfy_password = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
}
```

## 4. Errors and fixes:
- **User feedback on darshan permissions**: Initially gave darshan `rw` access to all topics. User pointed out darshan only needs to subscribe, not publish. Fixed by changing to `ro` (read-only).
- **User request for n8n service account**: User mentioned they added n8n_password to 1Password. Added n8n user to provisioning playbook with `rw` on `docker-updates` topic.
- **User preference for Ansible over shell script**: Originally created a shell script for provisioning. User asked to use Ansible instead. Replaced with `ansible_navigator_run` resource and YAML playbook template.

- Researched ntfy ACL documentation to understand permission model
- Designed user/role structure with principle of least privilege
- Integrated with existing 1Password workflow using section-based field extraction
- Used Docker secrets for Alertmanager password (password_file approach)

I think we should revisit our ntfy auth. maybe we can setup access control for our topics"

# Notification Configuration in AutoKuma

Based on the provided documentation, here's what's available about notification configuration:

## Basic Configuration

AutoKuma supports notification provider definitions through container labels. The documentation notes that **"Defining Notifications is currently experimental and might change in the future."**

## Label Format

Notifications follow this pattern:
```
kuma.<id>.notification.<setting>: <value>
```

## Example Configuration

The documentation provides one concrete example:

```yaml
kuma.mynotificationprovider.notification.name: 'This is a Matrix notification provider'
kuma.mynotificationprovider.notification.active: 'true'
kuma.mynotificationprovider.notification.config: '{"type": "matrix", "accessToken": "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", "homeserverUrl": "https://matrix.org", "internalRoomId": "!xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx:matrix.org"}'
```

## Usage with Monitors

Once defined, notification providers can be assigned to monitors via:
```
kuma.<monitor_id>.http.notification_name_list: '["mynotificationprovider"]'
```

## Important Notes

The documentation does **not** include ntfy examples or a comprehensive list of supported notification types. For detailed notification configuration options and additional provider types, you would need to consult the referenced entity types documentation or the Uptime Kuma API documentation.

Based on my search, here's what I found about Uptime Kuma and ntfy notification configuration with JSON API format:

## Uptime Kuma ntfy Notification Configuration

### Native Integration
Uptime Kuma now allows publishing to ntfy, with built-in support for the notification type.

### Configuration Options (via uptime-kuma-api)
The ntfy notification type in Uptime Kuma supports these parameters:
- **ntfyAuthenticationMethod** - Authentication Method
- **ntfyusername** and **ntfypassword** - Username/password credentials
- **ntfyaccesstoken** - Access Token
- **ntfytopic** - The ntfy topic
- **ntfyPriority** - Priority level
- **ntfyserverurl** - Server URL
- **ntfyIcon** - Icon for notifications

### JSON API Format for ntfy
When publishing via HTTP POST to ntfy, the JSON format includes fields like: topic, message, title, tags (array), and priority. Example structure:
```json
{
  "topic": "uptimekuma",
  "message": "Site is down",
  "title": "Site Down Alert",
  "tags": ["warning","loudspeaker"],
  "priority": 4
}
```

### Important Notes for JSON Publishing
"JSON publishing is only possible, when POST-ing to the root URL of the ntfy instance."(no content)When sending as JSON (application/json), make sure to send the JSON POST request to ntfy.domain.com without the topic name in the url and include the "topic" name in the JSON body.

### API Documentation
In Uptime Kuma's API, notifications use a NotificationObject where Config is stringified JSON, with a notificationID for identification.

### Known Issue
Some users have reported that notifications received in the ntfy android app appear as the actual JSON string, like: {"topic":"Alert", "title": "Alert [Uptime-Kuma]", "message": "Ntfy alert Testing", "priority":3, "tags":["test_tube"]} - this is typically a configuration issue related to content-type headers.

# Ntfy Notification Configuration

Based on the documentation, here are the ntfy notification parameters:

## Required Fields
- **name** (str): Friendly name for the notification
- **type**: `NotificationType.NTFY`
- **ntfyAuthenticationMethod** (str): Authentication method
- **ntfyusername** (str): Username
- **ntfypassword** (str): Password
- **ntfyaccesstoken** (str): Access token
- **ntfyIcon** (str): Icon identifier

## Optional Fields
- **ntfytopic** (str): Topic name
- **ntfyPriority** (int): Message priority level
- **ntfyserverurl** (str): Custom server URL

## Example Usage

```python
api.add_notification(
    name="ntfy_alert",
    type=NotificationType.NTFY,
    ntfyAuthenticationMethod="token",
    ntfyusername="user",
    ntfypassword="pass",
    ntfyaccesstoken="token_value",
    ntfytopic="my-topic",
    ntfyPriority=5,
    ntfyIcon="bell",
    ntfyserverurl="https://ntfy.sh"
)
```

The same parameters apply to both `test_notification()` and `edit_notification()` methods.

I see the current monitors.json is static. However, AutoKuma's notification support uses Docker labels format, not JSON. Looking at the docker-compose environment variables:

```
AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
```

AutoKuma has two modes:
1. **Docker labels** - can define notifications with `kuma.<id>.notification.*` labels
2. **Static JSON file** - monitors only, notifications not supported in JSON format

Since you're using the static JSON file approach, **notifications cannot be configured declaratively in the current setup**. The experimental notification support is only available via Docker labels.

You have two options:

**Option 1: Manual Configuration** (simplest)
Configure the ntfy notification once in Uptime Kuma UI. It will persist across restarts since the data is stored in the mounted volume.

**Option 2: Switch to Docker Labels** (more complex)
Replace the static JSON with Docker labels on the AutoKuma container itself. This would require restructuring the configuration significantly and the notification support is still experimental.

Given that:
- Notification configuration is a one-time setup
- AutoKuma notification support is experimental
- The monitors.json approach is cleaner for your current setup

I recommend **Option 1** - configure ntfy notification manually in the Uptime Kuma UI after deployment. You'll need to:

1. Go to **Settings → Notifications → Setup Notification**
2. Select **ntfy** as the notification type
3. Configure:
   - **Server URL**: `http://ntfy:80` (internal Docker network)
   - **Topic**: `homelab-alerts`
   - **Authentication Method**: Username and Password
   - **Username**: Create a new service account `uptime-kuma` or reuse `alertmanager`
   - **Password**: The corresponding password from 1Password

Do you want me to add an `uptime-kuma` service account to the ntfy provisioning playbook, or would you prefer to reuse the `alertmanager` account since both send to `homelab-alerts`?

Sounds good! Just to summarize what you'll need to do:

**1. Deploy the changes:**
```bash
task tofu:plan APP=monitoring
task tofu:apply APP=monitoring
```

**2. Configure Uptime Kuma notification (one-time in UI):**
- Go to **Settings → Notifications → Setup Notification**
- Type: **ntfy**
- Server URL: `http://ntfy:80`
- Topic: `homelab-alerts`
- Authentication: Username/Password
- Username: `alertmanager` (reuse existing account)
- Password: Same as `alertmanager_password` from 1Password

The Ansible provisioner will automatically run after the container deploys to create all the ntfy users and ACL rules. You can verify with:

```

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"

    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)
