# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]

  # Pass env content to module - synced BEFORE docker compose runs
  env_content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = local.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = local.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = local.op.uptime_kuma_password
    discord_webhook_url    = local.op.discord_webhook_url
    # Grafana OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
    grafana_oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.grafana.client_id
    grafana_oauth_client_secret = random_password.grafana_oidc_secret.result
    grafana_oauth_auth_url      = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/authorize/"
    grafana_oauth_token_url     = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/token/"
    grafana_oauth_api_url       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/userinfo/"
    grafana_oauth_signout_url   = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/grafana/end-session/"
    # ntfy credentials for Alertmanager
    ntfy_alertmanager_password = local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password
    # ntfy credentials for Discord forwarder
    ntfy_discord_forwarder_password = local.op.ntfy_discord_forwarder_password
  })
}

# Note: .env file is now handled by the docker-lxc module via env_content
# This ensures the .env is synced BEFORE docker compose runs

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ntfy User Provisioning (Ansible)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provisions ntfy users and ACL after container deployment

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "ntfy_provision" {
  triggers = {
    container_id = module.monitoring.container_id
    container_ip = module.monitoring.ip_address
    # Re-run if credentials change
    credentials_hash = sha256(join(",", [
      local.op.ntfy_admin_password,
      local.op.ntfy_darshan_password,
      local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password,
      local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password,
      local.op.ntfy_n8n_password,
      local.op.ntfy_uptime_kuma_password,
      local.op.ntfy_discord_forwarder_password,
    ]))
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/ntfy/provision-users.yml.tpl", {
    ntfy_admin_user                 = local.op.ntfy_admin_user
    ntfy_admin_password             = local.op.ntfy_admin_password
    ntfy_darshan_password           = local.op.ntfy_darshan_password
    ntfy_alertmanager_password      = local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password
    ntfy_pbs_backup_password        = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
    ntfy_n8n_password               = local.op.ntfy_n8n_password
    ntfy_uptime_kuma_password       = local.op.ntfy_uptime_kuma_password
    ntfy_discord_forwarder_password = local.op.ntfy_discord_forwarder_password
  })

  inventory = yamlencode({
    monitoring = {
      hosts = {
        "monitoring" = {
          ansible_host = module.monitoring.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "grafana_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "grafana"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "grafana.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "prometheus_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prometheus"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9090"

  internal_domain = "prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "alertmanager_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "alertmanager"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9093"

  internal_domain = "alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "uptime_kuma_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "status"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3001"

  internal_domain = "status.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "ntfy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # ntfy has its own ACL-based authentication - no Authentik middleware
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.monitoring.container_id
  container_ip   = module.monitoring.ip_address
  container_name = "monitoring"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "4"          # Keep 4 weekly backups

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,monitoring"
    ntfy_user     = "pbs-backup"
    ntfy_password = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.monitoring.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.monitoring.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.monitoring.ssh_command
}

output "alloy_endpoints" {
  value = {
    grpc = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4317"
    http = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4318"
  }
}

output "loki_url" {
  value = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3100"
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.internal_url
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.internal_url
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.internal_url
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.internal_url
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.remote_config_path
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.remote_config_path
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.remote_config_path
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.remote_config_path
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Network Services LXC - AdGuard + Cloudflared + DDNS
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 101
#
# Core network infrastructure: DNS (AdGuard Home), Cloudflare tunnel, DDNS.
# Tailscale runs as systemd service (requires kernel access).
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 101
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "cloudflare_ddns_domains" {
  type    = string
  default = "homelab.rambtech.dev"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Network Services Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "network_services" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "network-services"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for DNS service)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.core.network_services}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.network_services}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for Tailscale kernel access
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude AdGuard config - managed separately via templating for dns_mode toggle
  exclude_patterns = ["AdGuardHome\\.yaml$", "\\.tpl$"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Network Services"
  service_description = "Core network infrastructure: DNS, tunnels, and VPN"

  service_urls = {
    adguard_internal = "https://dns.${var.domain_internal}"
    adguard_direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.network_services}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "AdGuard Home", port = 53, info = "DNS server with ad blocking" },
    { name = "AdGuard UI", port = 3000, info = "Web management interface" },
    { name = "Cloudflared", port = 0, info = "Cloudflare tunnel (outbound only)" },
    { name = "Tailscale", port = 41641, info = "Mesh VPN (systemd service)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Tailscale Management

Tailscale runs as a systemd service (not Docker) because it requires kernel-level network access.

**Check status:**
```bash
systemctl status tailscaled
tailscale status
```

**Restart if needed:**
```bash
systemctl restart tailscaled
```

## Docker Services

**View logs:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose logs -f <service>
```

**Restart all services:**
```bash
cd /config && docker compose restart
```

## DNS Testing

**Test AdGuard (port 53):**
```bash
dig @${local.lan_ips.network_services} google.com
```

**Test internal DNS rewrites:**
```bash
dig @${local.lan_ips.network_services} traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=network-services` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["network-services", "dns", "adguard", "cloudflare"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "network_services_env" {
  content = <<-EOT
# Network Services Environment Variables
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Cloudflare Tunnel Token
CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=${local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token}

# Cloudflare API Token for DDNS
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=${local.op.cloudflare_api_token}

# Domains to update with DDNS
CLOUDFLARE_DDNS_DOMAINS=${var.cloudflare_ddns_domains}
EOT

  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/network-services.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "network_services_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.network_services_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.network_services.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.network_services]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AdGuard Home Configuration (DNS Mode Toggle)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generates AdGuard config based on dns_mode variable:
# - home: Uses LAN IPs (192.168.1.x) - works on home network without Tailscale
# - travel: Uses container IPs (10.100.x.x) - routes through Tailscale, avoids subnet conflicts

locals {
  # Select IP based on dns_mode
  adguard_traefik_ip = var.dns_mode == "travel" ? local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik : local.lan_ips.traefik
}

resource "local_file" "adguard_config" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/adguard/conf/AdGuardHome.yaml.tpl", {
    dns_mode   = var.dns_mode
    traefik_ip = local.adguard_traefik_ip
  })

  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/AdGuardHome.yaml"
  file_permission = "0644"
}

resource "filesync_file" "adguard_config" {
  source      = local_file.adguard_config.filename
  destination = "/config/adguard/conf/AdGuardHome.yaml"
  host        = module.network_services.ip_address

  mode = "0644"

  depends_on = [module.network_services]
}

# Restart AdGuard when config changes
resource "null_resource" "restart_adguard" {
  triggers = {
    config_hash = local_file.adguard_config.content_md5
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "docker restart adguard || true"
    ]

    connection {
      type        = "ssh"
      user        = "root"
      host        = module.network_services.ip_address
      private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }
  }

  depends_on = [filesync_file.adguard_config]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tailscale Service Management via Ansible
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensures Tailscale daemon is running and connected after deployment

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "manage_tailscale" {
  depends_on = [module.network_services]

  # Re-run when container is rebuilt or network config changes
  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
    lan_ip       = local.lan_ips.network_services
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false  # Run ansible directly on host
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = <<-EOT
    - name: Manage Tailscale service on network-services
      hosts: lxc
      gather_facts: no
      vars:
        app_name: network-services

      tasks:
        # =====================================================================
        # Tailscale Service Management
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Ensure Tailscale daemon is running
          ansible.builtin.systemd:
            name: tailscaled
            state: started
            enabled: true
          register: tailscale_service

        - name: Wait for Tailscale to initialize
          ansible.builtin.pause:
            seconds: 3
          when: tailscale_service.changed

        # =====================================================================
        # Verify Tailscale Status
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Check Tailscale connection status
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: tailscale status --json
          register: tailscale_status
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: false

        - name: Parse Tailscale status
          ansible.builtin.set_fact:
            tailscale_info: "{{ tailscale_status.stdout | from_json }}"
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Display Tailscale connection info
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: |
              Tailscale Status: {{ 'Connected' if (tailscale_info.BackendState | default('')) == 'Running' else 'Not Connected' }}
              Tailnet IP: {{ tailscale_info.Self.TailscaleIPs[0] | default('N/A') }}
              Hostname: {{ tailscale_info.Self.HostName | default('N/A') }}
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Warn if Tailscale not connected
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: "WARNING: Tailscale is not connected. Check authentication status with 'tailscale status'"
          when: tailscale_status.rc != 0 or (tailscale_info.BackendState | default('')) != 'Running'
  EOT

    lxc = {
      hosts = {
        "network-services" = {
          ansible_host = module.network_services.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}

**Option 1: Export JSON to repo (Recommended)**
- Export workflows as JSON files to `tofu/apps/n8n/workflows/`

tofu/apps/n8n/

│   ├── docker-update-assistant.json    # New AI workflow

```

content.text:
Yes, exactly. Since n8n has a REST API, we could:

1. **Export workflow JSON to repo** (version controlled)
2. **Use Ansible/Tofu to push workflows via API** on deploy

The n8n API supports:
- `GET /api/v1/workflows` - list all
- `GET /api/v1/workflows/{id}` - get specific
- `POST /api/v1/workflows` - create new
- `PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id}` - update existing
- `POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/activate` - activate

So the flow would be:
```
tofu/apps/n8n/
├── workflows/
│   ├── docker-update-checker.json
│   └── docker-update-assistant.json
└── main.tf  # Ansible task to sync workflows via API
```

On `task tofu:apply APP=n8n`:
1. Ansible reads JSON files from `workflows/`
2. For each workflow, checks if it exists (by name or ID)
3. Creates or updates via API
4. Optionally activates

This gives you:
- **Version control** - diffs, history, code review
- **IaC deployment** - workflows deploy with infrastructure
- **Idempotent** - safe to run repeatedly

Want me to set this up? I can:
1. Check what API key/auth n8n needs
2. Export the existing Docker Update Checker workflow
3. Create the Ansible task in `main.tf`

content.text:
Great point. The challenge is bidirectional sync - we want both:
- **Push**: Deploy workflows from git → n8n
- **Pull**: Capture UI changes from n8n → git

**The problem with Tofu/Ansible**: They're designed for push-only. If you edit in n8n UI, Tofu won't know and will overwrite on next apply.

**Better approach: n8n workflow that syncs itself to git**

```
n8n UI change → Webhook trigger → Export workflow → Commit to git
```

n8n can:
1. Listen for workflow save events (webhook or schedule)
2. Export its own workflows via internal API
3. Commit changes to a git branch
4. Optionally create a PR for review

This way:
- UI changes automatically sync to git
- You review/merge PRs for workflow changes
- Tofu only handles n8n infrastructure, not workflow content

**Simpler alternative: Scheduled export + alert**

A cron workflow in n8n that:
1. Exports all workflows daily
2. Compares to last export
3. If changed, sends ntfy alert: "n8n workflows changed - run export script"

Then you manually pull and commit when notified.

Which approach interests you more?
1. **Fully automated** - n8n commits its own changes to git
2. **Semi-automated** - n8n alerts you, you run an export script
3. **Manual** - Just document the export process, run when needed

content.text:
Interesting idea. Looking at how `filesync_file` works currently - it's one-way (local → remote). You're suggesting adding a "pull" mode.

But there's a fundamental issue: **Tofu state expects to be the source of truth**. If the remote changes independently, Tofu sees drift and wants to "fix" it by pushing local again.

**What we'd actually need:**

A separate resource type, something like `filesync_sync` that:
1. On `plan`: Compares local ↔ remote, shows diff either direction
2. On `apply`: 
   - If `direction = "push"`: local → remote (current behavior)
   - If `direction = "pull"`: remote → local
   - If `direction = "bidirectional"`: merge somehow (complex)

## Comprehensive Summary: terraform-provider-filesync

### 1. Overall Project Structure

**Location**: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/terraform-provider-filesync`

The provider is a Terraform/OpenTofu native provider (not a provisioner) for declarative file synchronization via SSH/SFTP. It treats files as first-class Terraform resources with proper state tracking.

**Key Files**:
- `main.go` - Entry point, initializes provider server
- `go.mod` - Dependencies (Terraform Plugin Framework v1.17.0, gosftp custom library, testing framework)
- `internal/provider/` - Core provider logic
- `internal/diff/` - Diff generation utilities
- `tests/acceptance/` - Integration tests with testcontainers
- `examples/` - Usage examples

### 2. Resource Implementation: filesync_file

**File**: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/terraform-provider-filesync/internal/provider/file_resource.go` (~800 lines)

#### Data Model
```
FileResourceModel:
  - source (required)        # Local file path
  - destination (required)   # Remote absolute path
  - host (required)          # Remote host (IP/hostname)
  - SSH settings (optional)  # ssh_user, ssh_key_path, ssh_private_key, ssh_port, ssh_password, ssh_certificate, ssh_certificate_path
  - Bastion settings        # For multi-hop SSH
  - Security settings       # insecure_ignore_host_key, known_hosts_file, strict_host_key_checking
  - File attributes         # owner, group, mode (Unix permissions)
  - Computed attributes     # id, source_hash, size
```

#### CRUD Operations

**Create** (lines 322-393):
1. Calculate SHA256 hash of source file
2. Create SSH client connection (with connection pool support if enabled)
3. Upload file via SFTP
4. Set file ownership and permissions
5. Store computed values: ID (host:destination), SourceHash (sha256:hex), Size
6. Save to state

**Read** (lines 395-437):
- Validates source file still exists locally
- If source deleted → removes resource from state
- **KEY**: Does NOT update `source_hash` from remote; preserves state hash to allow plan-time change detection
- This allows Terraform to detect local changes during plan phase

**Update** (lines 439-571):
1. Calculate new source file hash
2. Create SSH client
3. **DRIFT DETECTION**: Compare remote file hash against stored state hash
   - If drift detected → fails with detailed error message including content diff
   - If no drift → proceeds with upload
4. Upload file and set attributes
5. Update state with new hash

**Delete** (lines 573-605):
1. Create SSH client
2. Delete remote file via SFTP
3. Remove from state

#### Import (lines 607-654)
- Format: `host:destination` (e.g., `192.168.1.100:/etc/config.json`)
- Parses ID to extract host and destination
- User must manually add `source` attribute to config
- Next apply syncs state with config

#### Plan-Time Hash Computation (lines 729-803)

Custom plan modifiers (`sourceHashPlanModifier`, `sourceSizePlanModifier`):
- Compute local file hash during planning phase
- Set plan value to current local hash
- If differs from state → triggers Update action in terraform plan
- **Enables plan-time change detection without remote connection**

### 3. Resource Implementation: filesync_directory

**File**: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/terraform-provider-filesync/internal/provider/directory_resource.go` (~1255 lines)

Similar to filesync_file but for directories with advanced features:

#### Data Model
```
DirectoryResourceModel:
  - All filesync_file attributes
  - Sync options:
    - exclude (patterns)          # Glob patterns to skip files
    - parallel_uploads (1-32)     # Default: 4 concurrent uploads
    - symlink_policy (follow/skip/preserve)
  - Computed:
    - file_count                  # Number of synced files
    - total_size                  # Sum of all file sizes
    - file_hashes (map)           # Individual file hashes
```

#### Key Features

**Directory Scanning** (lines 970-1052):
- Recursively walks directory structure
- Calculates SHA256 hash for each file
- Supports exclude patterns (glob matching on filename, path, and components)
- Handles symlinks: follow (hash content), skip (ignore), preserve (store target path)
- Sorts files consistently

**Update Logic** (lines 511-691):
1. Scans local directory (with excludes/symlink policies)
2. Gets previous file hashes from state
3. **Categorization**:
   - Unchanged files (no upload if attributes also unchanged)
   - Changed files (upload)
   - Deleted files (remote deletion)
4. **Parallel uploads** (lines 883-957):
   - Worker pool pattern with configurable parallelism
   - Each worker uploads file, sets attributes
   - Collects results and errors
5. Updates file_hashes map and combined hash

**Combined Hash** (lines 1077-1087):
- SHA256 of concatenated individual file hashes
- Detects any change in any file or file set

#### Plan Modifiers (lines 1145-1254)
Four separate modifiers compute during planning:
- `directorySourceHashPlanModifier` - Combined hash
- `directoryFileCountPlanModifier` - File count
- `directoryTotalSizePlanModifier` - Total size
- `directoryFileHashesPlanModifier` - File hashes map

All use `scanDirectoryForPlan()` helper to compute values locally without remote connection.

### 4. State and Drift Detection

**State Tracking**:
- File hash stored in state represents what was last synced
- Enables plan-time detection (local file change) vs drift detection (remote change)

**Drift Detection Flow** (file_resource.go lines 478-533):
1. During Update, hash remote file
2. Compare against state hash
3. If mismatch → drift detected
4. Fetch both files (up to 100KB) for content diff
5. Format detailed error message with:
   - Hashes (expected vs found)
   - Content diff (unified format)
   - Resolution suggestions

**Diff Utility** (`internal/diff/diff.go`):
- Uses `github.com/sergi/go-diff` (diffmatchpatch)
- Limits to 100KB files, skips binary content
- Unified diff format with context lines
- Truncates to 50 lines max

### 5. SSH Configuration and Connection

**File**: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/terraform-provider-filesync/internal/provider/ssh_config.go`

**Authentication Methods** (BuildSSHConfig lines 75-181):
1. **Private Key** (priority order):
   - Resource-level `ssh_private_key` (inline content)
   - Resource-level `ssh_key_path` (file path with ~ expansion)
   - Provider default `ssh_private_key`
   - Provider default `ssh_key_path`

2. **Password**: Resource > Provider level

3. **Certificate**: Content or path, works with private key

4. **Bastion/Jump Host**: Full config (host, port, user, key/password)

**SSH Security** (lines 153-178):
- `insecure_ignore_host_key` - Skip verification (bool)
- `known_hosts_file` - Custom known_hosts (with ~ expansion)
- `strict_host_key_checking` - Mode: "yes" (default), "no", "accept-new"

**Connection Pooling** (provider.go lines 189-195):
- Optional per-provider: `connection_pool_enabled`
- Creates `gosftp.ConnectionPool` with 5-minute idle timeout
- Reuses SSH connections across resources
- Improves performance for multiple files on same host

**Retry Configuration**:
- `max_retries` (default: 3) - Retry transient SSH failures

### 6. SSH Client Interface

**Dependency**: Custom `github.com/darshan-rambhia/gosftp` library

**Key Methods Used**:
- `UploadFile(ctx, localPath, remotePath)` - SFTP upload
- `DeleteFile(ctx, remotePath)` - Delete remote file
- `SetFileAttributes(ctx, path, owner, group, mode)` - chown and chmod
- `GetFileHash(ctx, remotePath)` - SHA256 hash of remote file (for drift detection)
- `FileExists(ctx, remotePath)` - Check file existence
- `ReadFileContent(ctx, remotePath, maxSize)` - Read content for diff

**Connection Pool Interface**:
- `GetOrCreate(config)` - Retrieve or create connection
- `Release(config)` - Return connection to pool

### 7. Host Data Source

**File**: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/terraform-provider-filesync/internal/provider/host_datasource.go`

**Purpose**: Reusable host configuration for multiple resources

**Model**:
```
HostDataSourceModel:
  - address (required)         # Host IP/hostname
  - SSH settings (optional)    # Same as resources
  - Computed: id (host:<address>)
```

**Use Cases**:
- Define once, reference multiple times
- Use with `for_each` for multi-host deployments
- Password/certificate authentication patterns

### 8. Provider Configuration

**File**: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/terraform-provider-filesync/internal/provider/provider.go`

**Default Settings** (can be overridden per-resource):
- SSH defaults: user, key/password, certificate, port, bastion settings
- Security defaults: host key verification, known_hosts, strict checking
- Connection pooling: enabled/disabled
- Retry: max_retries (default: 3)

**Resource Registration** (lines 202-213):
- Registers `FileResource`
- Registers `DirectoryResource`
- Registers `HostDataSource`

### 9. Plan/Apply Flow Summary

```
PLAN PHASE:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Load current state                               │
│ 2. For each resource:                               │
│    - Read plan modifiers compute local file hash(es)│
│    - Compare against state hash                     │
│    - If different → mark for update in plan         │
│    - If deleted locally → mark for destroy          │
│ 3. NO REMOTE CONNECTION - plan is fast              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

APPLY PHASE:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. For each Create action:                          │
│    - Upload file                                    │
│    - Set attributes                                 │
│    - Store hash in state                            │
│                                                     │
│ 2. For each Update action:                          │
│    - Connect to remote                              │
│    - DRIFT CHECK: compare remote hash vs state      │
│    - If drift → FAIL with detailed error + diff     │
│    - If clean → upload file                         │
│    - Set attributes                                 │
│    - Update state hash                              │
│                                                     │
│ 3. For each Delete action:                          │
│    - Delete remote file                             │
│    - Remove from state                              │
│                                                     │
│ 4. Connection pooling returns connections to pool   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 10. Key Technical Highlights

1. **State Hash Strategy**: Stores hash of last synced state, not remote file
   - Enables plan-time change detection
   - Enables drift detection

2. **Parallel Directory Uploads**: Worker pool pattern with configurable parallelism
   - Concurrent SFTP sessions
   - Atomic result collection

3. **Drift Detection with Content Diff**: On detection, attempts to fetch both files and generate unified diff for user-friendly error messages

4. **Connection Pooling**: 5-minute idle timeout, reuse across resources

5. **Import Support**: Import existing remote files with `host:destination` format, then user adds source to config

6. **Plan Modifiers**: Custom Terraform Framework modifiers compute hashes locally during planning without remote connection

7. **Symlink Support**: Three policies for directory sync - follow (dereference), skip, preserve

### 11. Testing Structure

**Acceptance Tests** (`tests/acceptance/`):
- Uses testcontainers for ephemeral SSH servers
- Tests all CRUD operations
- Tests drift detection
- Tests directory features
- Tests connection pooling

**Unit Tests**:
- Individual resource tests
- Mock SSH client for isolation
- Validator tests

This architecture ensures Terraform manages files with proper state tracking, drift detection, and plan-time visibility while leveraging SFTP/SSH for secure transport.

### 9. Plan/Apply Flow Summary

```
PLAN PHASE:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Load current state                               │
│ 2. For each resource:                               │
│    - Read plan modifiers compute local file hash(es)│
│    - Compare against state hash                     │
│    - If different → mark for update in plan         │
│    - If deleted locally → mark for destroy          │
│ 3. NO REMOTE CONNECTION - plan is fast              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

APPLY PHASE:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. For each Create action:                          │
│    - Upload file                                    │
│    - Set attributes                                 │
│    - Store hash in state                            │

│ 2. For each Update action:                          │
│    - Connect to remote                              │

│    - Set attributes                                 │
│    - Update state hash                              │
│                                                     │
│ 3. For each Delete action:                          │
│    - Delete remote file                             │
│    - Remove from state                              │
│                                                     │
│ 4. Connection pooling returns connections to pool   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

   - Concurrent SFTP sessions

3. **Drift Detection with Content Diff**: On detection, attempts to fetch both files and generate unified diff for user-friendly error messages

4. **Connection Pooling**: 5-minute idle timeout, reuse across resources

5. **Import Support**: Import existing remote files with `host:destination` format, then user adds source to config

6. **Plan Modifiers**: Custom Terraform Framework modifiers compute hashes locally during planning without remote connection

7. **Symlink Support**: Three policies for directory sync - follow (dereference), skip, preserve

## Overview
Enhance the terraform-provider-filesync to support bidirectional awareness - detecting remote drift during plan and syncing local files from remote during import.

## Repository
`~/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/terraform-provider-filesync`

## Current Behavior
- **Plan**: Computes local hash, compares to state, detects local changes only
- **Apply**: Fetches remote hash, compares to state, fails on drift
- **Import**: Sets resource ID only, user must manually ensure local file matches

## Proposed Enhancements

### 1. Remote Drift Detection During Plan (`check_remote_on_plan`)

Add optional attribute to check remote during plan phase:

```hcl
resource "filesync_file" "workflow" {
  source      = "./workflows/docker-update.json"
  destination = "/config/workflow.json"
  host        = "10.100.5.102"
  
  # NEW: Check remote during plan to detect drift early
  check_remote_on_plan = true
}
```

**Implementation**:
- Add `check_remote_on_plan` boolean attribute (default: false)
- In plan modifier, if enabled:
  - Connect to remote via SSH/SFTP
  - Fetch remote file hash
  - Compare to state hash
  - If mismatch, add drift warning to plan diagnostics
- Consider caching connection across resources on same host

**Plan Output Example**:
```
~ filesync_file.workflow
    # WARNING: Remote file has drifted from state
    # Remote hash: sha256:abc123...
    # State hash:  sha256:def456...
    # Run 'tofu import' with import_syncs_local=true to accept remote changes
```

### 2. Import Syncs Local File (`import_syncs_local`)

Add attribute to pull remote content to local source during import:

```hcl
resource "filesync_file" "workflow" {
  source      = "./workflows/docker-update.json"
  destination = "/config/workflow.json"
  host        = "10.100.5.102"
  
  # NEW: On import, write remote content to source path
  import_syncs_local = true
}
```

**Implementation**:
- Add `import_syncs_local` boolean attribute (default: false)
- In ImportState function:
  1. Parse host:destination from import ID
  2. Connect to remote
  3. Read remote file content
  4. If `import_syncs_local` is true in config:
     - Write content to `source` path
     - Create parent directories if needed
  5. Compute hash of remote content
  6. Store in state: id, source_hash, destination, host
- Handle edge cases:
  - Source path doesn't exist yet (create it)
  - Source path exists but differs (overwrite with warning)
  - Remote file doesn't exist (error)

**Workflow**:
```bash
# 1. Add resource to config with import_syncs_local=true
# 2. Run import
tofu import filesync_file.workflow "10.100.5.102:/config/workflow.json"
# 3. Local file is created/updated from remote
# 4. State is in sync
# 5. Next plan shows no changes
```

## Use Case: n8n Workflow Management

This enables managing n8n workflows via IaC:
1. Edit workflow in n8n UI
2. Run `tofu import` to pull changes to local JSON file
3. Commit to git
4. Future applies push local → remote

## Files to Modify

- `internal/provider/file_resource.go`:
  - Add `check_remote_on_plan` and `import_syncs_local` to schema
  - Modify plan modifiers for remote check
  - Enhance ImportState for local sync
  
- `internal/provider/directory_resource.go`:
  - Same enhancements for directory resource

- `tests/acceptance/`:
  - Add tests for new attributes

## Considerations

- **Performance**: `check_remote_on_plan` adds SSH connection during plan
  - Mitigate with connection pooling
  - Document as opt-in for specific resources
  
- **Security**: Writing to local filesystem during import
  - Validate source path is within allowed directories?
  - Or trust user knows what they're doing (Terraform philosophy)

- **Atomicity**: If import fails mid-write, local file could be corrupted
  - Write to temp file, then atomic rename

## Related
- Bead proxmox-homelab-pdn (AI Docker Update Assistant) - needs this for n8n workflow sync

content.text: gosftp already has `ReadFileContent` which reads remote file content. Let me check if that's sufficient:

**gosftp already has what we need:**

| Method | Purpose | Import Use |
|--------|---------|------------|
| `ReadFileContent(ctx, path, maxBytes)` | Read remote file content | ✅ Fetch remote file |
| `GetFileHash(ctx, path)` | Get SHA256 of remote file | ✅ Drift detection |
| `FileExists(ctx, path)` | Check if remote exists | ✅ Validate before import |

For the import sync, the filesync provider can:
1. Call `FileExists()` to verify remote file exists
2. Call `ReadFileContent(ctx, path, 0)` to read full content (0 = no limit)
3. Write content to local `source` path
4. Call `GetFileHash()` to store in state

**No changes needed in gosftp.** The provider already has all the primitives it needs. The implementation is purely in `terraform-provider-filesync`.

One minor consideration: `ReadFileContent` with `maxBytes=0` means unlimited, but very large files could be an issue. For n8n workflows (JSON files), this is fine. If we wanted to be safer, we could add a configurable max size or stream to disk for large files - but that's an optimization for later.

   395→func (r *FileResource) Read(ctx context.Context, req resource.ReadRequest, resp *resource.ReadResponse) {
   396→	var data FileResourceModel
   397→
   398→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &data)...)
   399→	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
   400→		return
   401→	}
   402→
   403→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "id", data.ID.ValueString())
   404→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Reading file resource state")
   405→
   406→	// Read refreshes state from the resource.
   407→	// IMPORTANT: We do NOT update source_hash here. The source_hash represents
   408→	// what was last successfully synced to the remote, not the current local file.
   409→	// This allows Terraform to detect local file changes during plan.
   410→	//
   411→	// The plan modifier on source_hash computes the current local file hash
   412→	// and triggers an update when it differs from the stored state hash.
   413→
   414→	sourcePath := data.Source.ValueString()
   415→
   416→	// If source is not set (e.g., after import), don't remove from state.
   417→	// The user needs to update their config to include the source attribute.
   418→	if sourcePath == "" || data.Source.IsNull() || data.Source.IsUnknown() {
   419→		tflog.Debug(ctx, "Source path not set (possibly after import), preserving state")
   420→		// Preserve the current state - source will be set in next apply.
   421→		resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &data)...)
   422→		return
   423→	}
   424→
   425→	if _, err := os.Stat(sourcePath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
   426→		tflog.Info(ctx, "Source file no longer exists, removing resource from state", map[string]interface{}{
   427→			"source": sourcePath,
   428→		})
   429→		// Source file was deleted - remove from state.
   430→		resp.State.RemoveResource(ctx)
   431→		return
   432→	}
   433→
   434→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "File resource state preserved")
   435→	// State is unchanged - we preserve the existing source_hash.
   436→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &data)...)
   437→}

   439→func (r *FileResource) Update(ctx context.Context, req resource.UpdateRequest, resp *resource.UpdateResponse) {
   440→	var data FileResourceModel
   441→	var state FileResourceModel
   442→
   443→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.Plan.Get(ctx, &data)...)
   444→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
   445→	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
   446→		return
   447→	}
   448→
   449→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "host", data.Host.ValueString())
   450→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "source", data.Source.ValueString())
   451→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "destination", data.Destination.ValueString())
   452→
   453→	tflog.Info(ctx, "Updating file resource")
   454→
   455→	// Calculate new source file hash.
   456→	newHash, size, err := hashFile(data.Source.ValueString())
   457→	if err != nil {
   458→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to read source file", err.Error())
   459→		return
   460→	}
   461→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Computed new source file hash", map[string]interface{}{
   462→		"new_hash":  newHash,
   463→		"old_hash":  state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   464→		"size":      size,
   465→		"unchanged": newHash == state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   466→	})
   467→
   468→	// Create SSH client.
   469→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Establishing SSH connection")
   470→	client, err := r.createSSHClient(&data)
   471→	if err != nil {
   472→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to create SSH connection", err.Error())
   473→		return
   474→	}
   475→	defer r.releaseSSHClient(&data, client)
   476→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "SSH connection established")
   477→
   478→	// Check for remote drift - compare remote hash with what we expect from state.
   479→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Checking for remote drift")
   480→	remoteHash, err := client.GetFileHash(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString())
   481→	if err != nil {
   482→		// Check if file doesn't exist (could be first create after import).
   483→		// We need to distinguish between "file not found" and other errors.
   484→		exists, existsErr := client.FileExists(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString())
   485→		if existsErr != nil {
   486→			// Can't even check if file exists - report the connection/permission issue.
   487→			resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   488→				"Failed to check remote file",
   489→				fmt.Sprintf("Could not verify remote file state at %s: %v", data.Destination.ValueString(), existsErr),
   490→			)
   491→			return
   492→		}
   493→		if exists {
   494→			// File exists but we can't read it - permission issue.
   495→			resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   496→				"Cannot read remote file",
   497→				fmt.Sprintf("Remote file %s exists but cannot be read (permission denied?): %v", data.Destination.ValueString(), err),
   498→			)
   499→			return
   500→		}
   501→		tflog.Debug(ctx, "Remote file does not exist (first upload after import)")
   502→		// File doesn't exist - this is OK for first create after import, continue with upload.
   503→	} else if remoteHash != state.SourceHash.ValueString() {
   504→		tflog.Warn(ctx, "Remote file drift detected", map[string]interface{}{
   505→			"expected_hash": state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   506→			"remote_hash":   remoteHash,
   507→		})
   508→		// Drift detected! Try to generate a content diff for better error message
   509→		var diffContent string
   510→
   511→		// Read local file content for diff.
   512→		localContent, localErr := os.ReadFile(data.Source.ValueString())
   513→		if localErr == nil {
   514→			// Read remote file content for diff (limit to 100KB).
   515→			remoteContent, remoteErr := client.ReadFileContent(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString(), diff.MaxDiffSize)
   516→			if remoteErr == nil {
   517→				diffContent = diff.GenerateUnifiedDiff(localContent, remoteContent, data.Destination.ValueString())
   518→			}
   519→		}
   520→
   521→		errorMsg := diff.FormatDriftError(
   522→			data.ID.ValueString(),
   523→			data.Destination.ValueString(),
   524→			state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   525→			remoteHash,
   526→			diffContent,
   527→		)
   528→
   529→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Remote file drift detected", errorMsg)
   530→		return
   531→	} else {
   532→		tflog.Debug(ctx, "No remote drift detected")
   533→	}
   534→
   535→	// Upload file.
   536→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Uploading file")
   537→	if err := client.UploadFile(ctx, data.Source.ValueString(), data.Destination.ValueString()); err != nil {
   538→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to upload file", err.Error())
   539→		return
   540→	}
   541→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "File uploaded successfully")
   542→
   543→	// Set ownership and permissions.
   544→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Setting file attributes", map[string]interface{}{
   545→		"owner": data.Owner.ValueString(),
   546→		"group": data.Group.ValueString(),
   547→		"mode":  data.Mode.ValueString(),
   548→	})
   549→	if err := client.SetFileAttributes(
   550→		ctx,
   551→		data.Destination.ValueString(),
   552→		data.Owner.ValueString(),
   553→		data.Group.ValueString(),
   554→		data.Mode.ValueString(),
   555→	); err != nil {
   556→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to set file attributes", err.Error())
   557→		return
   558→	}
   559→
   560→	// Update computed values.
   561→	data.ID = types.StringValue(fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", data.Host.ValueString(), data.Destination.ValueString()))
   562→	data.SourceHash = types.StringValue(newHash)
   563→	data.Size = types.Int64Value(size)
   564→
   565→	tflog.Info(ctx, "File resource updated successfully", map[string]interface{}{
   566→		"id":   data.ID.ValueString(),
   567→		"size": size,
   568→	})
   569→
   570→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &data)...)
   571→}

   607→func (r *FileResource) ImportState(ctx context.Context, req resource.ImportStateRequest, resp *resource.ImportStateResponse) {
   608→	// Import format: "host:destination".
   609→	// Example: "192.168.1.100:/etc/myapp/config.json"
   610→	//
   611→	// After import, the user must update the config to set:.
   612→	// - source (required): path to the local source file
   613→	// - ssh_key_path or ssh_private_key (required): SSH credentials
   614→	//
   615→	// Then run `terraform apply` to sync state with the config.
   616→
   617→	id := req.ID
   618→	tflog.Info(ctx, "Importing file resource", map[string]interface{}{
   619→		"import_id": id,
   620→	})
   621→
   622→	// Parse the import ID - format is "host:destination".
   623→	// The destination is an absolute path, so we split on the first ":".
   624→	colonIdx := strings.Index(id, ":")
   625→	if colonIdx == -1 || colonIdx == 0 || colonIdx == len(id)-1 {
   626→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   627→			"Invalid Import ID",
   628→			fmt.Sprintf(
   629→				"Import ID must be in format 'host:destination' (e.g., '192.168.1.100:/etc/myapp/config.json').\n"+
   630→					"Got: %s", id,
   631→			),
   632→		)
   633→		return
   634→	}
   635→
   636→	host := id[:colonIdx]
   637→	destination := id[colonIdx+1:]
   638→
   639→	// Validate destination is an absolute path.
   640→	if !strings.HasPrefix(destination, "/") {
   641→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   642→			"Invalid Import ID",
   643→			fmt.Sprintf(
   644→				"Destination must be an absolute path starting with '/'.\n"+
   645→					"Got: %s", destination,
   646→			),
   647→		)
   648→		return
   649→	}
   650→
   651→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.SetAttribute(ctx, path.Root("id"), id)...)
   652→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.SetAttribute(ctx, path.Root("host"), host)...)
   653→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.SetAttribute(ctx, path.Root("destination"), destination)...)
   654→}

Now I need to implement the remote drift detection in the plan modifier. The challenge is that plan modifiers don't have access to the provider config (for SSH credentials). Let me check how to handle this.

Looking at the code, the plan modifier `sourceHashPlanModifier` is a struct with no access to the resource or provider. We need a different approach - either:
1. Store provider config in a package-level variable (not great)
2. Use a custom plan modifier that carries the resource reference
3. Use the Read function instead, which runs during refresh

Actually, the cleanest approach is to check drift in the `Read` function during `terraform refresh` or `terraform plan -refresh-only`. But for `check_remote_on_plan`, we want it during normal plan.

Let me create a custom plan modifier that can access the resource:

lines: +// remoteDriftChecker is used to check for remote drift during the Read phase.
+// This is called when check_remote_on_plan is true.
+// Note: We can't check during plan modifiers because they don't have access to
+// provider config (SSH credentials). Instead, we check during Read which runs
+// as part of refresh during plan.
+func (r *FileResource) checkRemoteDrift(ctx context.Context, data *FileResourceModel) (hasDrift bool, remoteHash string, err error) {
+  // Skip if check_remote_on_plan is not enabled.
+  // Skip if we don't have state hash to compare against.
+    return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create SSH connection for drift check: %w", err)
+    return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to check if remote file exists: %w", err)
+    // File doesn't exist on remote - this is drift (file was deleted).
+    return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get remote file hash: %w", err)

resp.Schema = schema.Schema{
		MarkdownDescription: `
Manages a single file on a remote host via SSH/SFTP.

## Behavior

- **Plan**: Compares local file hash against state. Shows change if local file modified.
- **Apply**:
  1. Connects to remote host via SSH
  2. Checks remote file hash against state (drift detection)
  3. If remote was modified externally, fails with error showing diff
  4. If no drift, uploads new file content
  5. Sets ownership and permissions
  6. Updates state with new hash

## Drift Detection

If someone modifies the remote file outside of Terraform, apply will fail:

` + "```" + `
Error: Remote file drift detected

  Resource: filesync_file.config
  File: /etc/myapp/app.conf

  Expected (from state): sha256:abc123...
  Found (on remote):     sha256:def456...

  To resolve:
    - terraform refresh   # Accept remote as source of truth
    - terraform apply -replace=filesync_file.config  # Force overwrite
` + "```" + `

## Example Usage

` + "```hcl" + `
resource "filesync_file" "nginx_config" {
  source      = "${path.module}/configs/nginx.conf"
  destination = "/etc/nginx/nginx.conf"
  host        = "192.168.1.100"

  owner = "root"
  group = "root"
  mode  = "0644"

  ssh_user     = "deploy"
  ssh_key_path = "~/.ssh/deploy_key"
}
` + "```" + `

  2. Checks remote file hash against state (drift detection)
  3. If remote was modified externally, fails with error showing diff
  4. If no drift, uploads new file content
  5. Sets ownership and permissions
  6. Updates state with new hash

The core implementation is done. Let me provide a summary of what was implemented:

## Implementation Summary

### New Features Added to `filesync_file` resource:

**1. `check_remote_on_plan` (boolean, optional)**
- When `true`, connects to remote during `terraform plan` (via the Read function during refresh)
- Compares remote file hash against state hash
- If drift detected, shows a **warning** in plan output with:
  - Expected vs actual hashes
  - Resolution options (import with sync, or force replace)
- Default: `false` (no remote check during plan)

**2. `import_syncs_local` (boolean, optional)**  
- When `true` and importing a resource:
  - Downloads remote file content via SFTP
  - Creates parent directories if needed
  - Writes content atomically to the local `source` path
  - Updates state with the hash of the synced content
- Triggers on post-import Read when:
  - `import_syncs_local = true`
  - `source_hash` is empty (fresh import)
  - Local file doesn't exist
- Default: `false` (standard import behavior)

### Usage Example for n8n Workflows:

```hcl
resource "filesync_file" "n8n_workflow" {
  source      = "${path.module}/workflows/docker-update-checker.json"
  destination = "/app/workflow.json"
  host        = "10.100.5.102"
  
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  
  # Enable bidirectional awareness
  check_remote_on_plan = true   # Warn about drift during plan
  import_syncs_local   = true   # Pull remote to local on import
}
```

**Workflow:**
1. Edit workflow in n8n UI
2. Run `tofu import filesync_file.n8n_workflow "10.100.5.102:/app/workflow.json"`
3. Local file is created/updated with remote content
4. Commit to git
5. Future plans will show if local or remote drifts

   379→func (r *FileResource) Create(ctx context.Context, req resource.CreateRequest, resp *resource.CreateResponse) {
   380→	var data FileResourceModel
   381→
   382→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.Plan.Get(ctx, &data)...)
   383→	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
   384→		return
   385→	}
   386→
   387→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "host", data.Host.ValueString())
   388→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "source", data.Source.ValueString())
   389→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "destination", data.Destination.ValueString())
   390→
   391→	tflog.Info(ctx, "Creating file resource")
   392→
   393→	// Calculate source file hash.
   394→	hash, size, err := hashFile(data.Source.ValueString())
   395→	if err != nil {
   396→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to read source file", err.Error())
   397→		return
   398→	}
   399→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Computed source file hash", map[string]interface{}{
   400→		"hash": hash,
   401→		"size": size,
   402→	})
   403→
   404→	// Create SSH client.
   405→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Establishing SSH connection")
   406→	client, err := r.createSSHClient(&data)
   407→	if err != nil {
   408→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to create SSH connection", err.Error())
   409→		return
   410→	}
   411→	defer r.releaseSSHClient(&data, client)
   412→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "SSH connection established")
   413→
   414→	// Upload file.
   415→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Uploading file")
   416→	if err := client.UploadFile(ctx, data.Source.ValueString(), data.Destination.ValueString()); err != nil {
   417→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to upload file", err.Error())
   418→		return
   419→	}
   420→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "File uploaded successfully")
   421→
   422→	// Set ownership and permissions.

   452→func (r *FileResource) Read(ctx context.Context, req resource.ReadRequest, resp *resource.ReadResponse) {
   453→	var data FileResourceModel
   454→
   455→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &data)...)
   456→	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
   457→		return
   458→	}
   459→
   460→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "id", data.ID.ValueString())
   461→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Reading file resource state")
   462→
   463→	// Read refreshes state from the resource.
   464→	// IMPORTANT: We do NOT update source_hash here. The source_hash represents
   465→	// what was last successfully synced to the remote, not the current local file.
   466→	// This allows Terraform to detect local file changes during plan.
   467→	//
   468→	// The plan modifier on source_hash computes the current local file hash
   469→	// and triggers an update when it differs from the stored state hash.
   470→
   471→	sourcePath := data.Source.ValueString()
   472→
   473→	// If source is not set (e.g., after import), don't remove from state.
   474→	// The user needs to update their config to include the source attribute.
   475→	if sourcePath == "" || data.Source.IsNull() || data.Source.IsUnknown() {
   476→		tflog.Debug(ctx, "Source path not set (possibly after import), preserving state")
   477→		// Preserve the current state - source will be set in next apply.
   478→		resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &data)...)
   479→		return
   480→	}
   481→
   482→	// Check if this is a post-import situation where we need to sync local from remote.
   483→	// Conditions:
   484→	// 1. import_syncs_local is true
   485→	// 2. source_hash is empty/null (indicates fresh import or never synced)
   486→	// 3. Local file doesn't exist OR differs from what we expect
   487→	localFileExists := true
   488→	if _, err := os.Stat(sourcePath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
   489→		localFileExists = false
   490→	}
   491→
   492→	shouldSyncFromRemote := !data.ImportSyncsLocal.IsNull() &&
   493→		data.ImportSyncsLocal.ValueBool() &&
   494→		(data.SourceHash.IsNull() || data.SourceHash.ValueString() == "") &&
   495→		!localFileExists
   496→
   497→	if shouldSyncFromRemote {
   498→		tflog.Info(ctx, "Post-import sync: downloading remote file to local source path")
   499→		if err := r.syncLocalFromRemote(ctx, &data); err != nil {
   500→			resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   501→				"Failed to sync local file from remote",
   502→				fmt.Sprintf("import_syncs_local is enabled but sync failed: %v", err),
   503→			)
   504→			return
   505→		}
   506→
   507→		// After syncing, compute the hash of the now-local file and update state.
   508→		hash, size, err := hashFile(sourcePath)
   509→		if err != nil {
   510→			resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   511→				"Failed to compute hash after sync",
   512→				fmt.Sprintf("Could not hash synced file %s: %v", sourcePath, err),
   513→			)
   514→			return
   515→		}
   516→
   517→		data.SourceHash = types.StringValue(hash)
   518→		data.Size = types.Int64Value(size)
   519→
   520→		tflog.Info(ctx, "Successfully synced local file and updated state", map[string]interface{}{
   521→			"source": sourcePath,
   522→			"hash":   hash,
   523→			"size":   size,
   524→		})
   525→
   526→		resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &data)...)
   527→		return
   528→	}
   529→
   530→	if !localFileExists {
   531→		tflog.Info(ctx, "Source file no longer exists, removing resource from state", map[string]interface{}{
   532→			"source": sourcePath,
   533→		})
   534→		// Source file was deleted - remove from state.
   535→		resp.State.RemoveResource(ctx)
   536→		return
   537→	}
   538→
   539→	// Check for remote drift if check_remote_on_plan is enabled.
   540→	hasDrift, remoteHash, err := r.checkRemoteDrift(ctx, &data)
   541→	if err != nil {
   542→		// Add warning but don't fail - drift check is informational.
   543→		resp.Diagnostics.AddWarning(
   544→			"Remote drift check failed",
   545→			fmt.Sprintf("Could not check remote file for drift: %v\n\n"+
   546→				"This may indicate connectivity issues. The apply will still check for drift.", err),
   547→		)
   548→	} else if hasDrift {
   549→		if remoteHash == "" {
   550→			resp.Diagnostics.AddWarning(
   551→				"Remote file missing",
   552→				fmt.Sprintf("Remote file %s does not exist but is expected.\n\n"+
   553→					"The file may have been deleted outside of Terraform.\n"+
   554→					"Run 'terraform apply' to recreate the file.",
   555→					data.Destination.ValueString()),
   556→			)
   557→		} else {
   558→			resp.Diagnostics.AddWarning(
   559→				"Remote file drift detected",
   560→				fmt.Sprintf("Remote file %s has been modified outside of Terraform.\n\n"+
   561→					"  Expected (from state): %s\n"+
   562→					"  Found (on remote):     %s\n\n"+
   563→					"To resolve:\n"+
   564→					"  - Run 'terraform apply' to overwrite remote with local (will fail with drift error)\n"+
   565→					"  - Run 'terraform apply -replace=%s' to force overwrite\n"+
   566→					"  - Run 'terraform import' with import_syncs_local=true to accept remote changes",
   567→					data.Destination.ValueString(),
   568→					data.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   569→					remoteHash,
   570→					fmt.Sprintf("filesync_file.%s", data.ID.ValueString())),
   571→			)
   572→		}
   573→	}
   574→
   575→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "File resource state preserved")
   576→	// State is unchanged - we preserve the existing source_hash.
   577→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &data)...)
   578→}

   580→func (r *FileResource) Update(ctx context.Context, req resource.UpdateRequest, resp *resource.UpdateResponse) {
   581→	var data FileResourceModel
   582→	var state FileResourceModel
   583→
   584→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.Plan.Get(ctx, &data)...)
   585→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
   586→	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
   587→		return
   588→	}
   589→
   590→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "host", data.Host.ValueString())
   591→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "source", data.Source.ValueString())
   592→	ctx = tflog.SetField(ctx, "destination", data.Destination.ValueString())
   593→
   594→	tflog.Info(ctx, "Updating file resource")
   595→
   596→	// Calculate new source file hash.
   597→	newHash, size, err := hashFile(data.Source.ValueString())
   598→	if err != nil {
   599→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to read source file", err.Error())
   600→		return
   601→	}
   602→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Computed new source file hash", map[string]interface{}{
   603→		"new_hash":  newHash,
   604→		"old_hash":  state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   605→		"size":      size,
   606→		"unchanged": newHash == state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   607→	})
   608→
   609→	// Create SSH client.
   610→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Establishing SSH connection")
   611→	client, err := r.createSSHClient(&data)
   612→	if err != nil {
   613→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to create SSH connection", err.Error())
   614→		return
   615→	}
   616→	defer r.releaseSSHClient(&data, client)
   617→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "SSH connection established")
   618→
   619→	// Check for remote drift - compare remote hash with what we expect from state.
   620→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Checking for remote drift")
   621→	remoteHash, err := client.GetFileHash(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString())
   622→	if err != nil {
   623→		// Check if file doesn't exist (could be first create after import).
   624→		// We need to distinguish between "file not found" and other errors.
   625→		exists, existsErr := client.FileExists(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString())
   626→		if existsErr != nil {
   627→			// Can't even check if file exists - report the connection/permission issue.
   628→			resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   629→				"Failed to check remote file",
   630→				fmt.Sprintf("Could not verify remote file state at %s: %v", data.Destination.ValueString(), existsErr),
   631→			)
   632→			return
   633→		}
   634→		if exists {
   635→			// File exists but we can't read it - permission issue.
   636→			resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   637→				"Cannot read remote file",
   638→				fmt.Sprintf("Remote file %s exists but cannot be read (permission denied?): %v", data.Destination.ValueString(), err),
   639→			)
   640→			return
   641→		}
   642→		tflog.Debug(ctx, "Remote file does not exist (first upload after import)")
   643→		// File doesn't exist - this is OK for first create after import, continue with upload.
   644→	} else if remoteHash != state.SourceHash.ValueString() {
   645→		tflog.Warn(ctx, "Remote file drift detected", map[string]interface{}{
   646→			"expected_hash": state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   647→			"remote_hash":   remoteHash,
   648→		})
   649→		// Drift detected! Try to generate a content diff for better error message
   650→		var diffContent string
   651→
   652→		// Read local file content for diff.
   653→		localContent, localErr := os.ReadFile(data.Source.ValueString())
   654→		if localErr == nil {
   655→			// Read remote file content for diff (limit to 100KB).
   656→			remoteContent, remoteErr := client.ReadFileContent(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString(), diff.MaxDiffSize)
   657→			if remoteErr == nil {
   658→				diffContent = diff.GenerateUnifiedDiff(localContent, remoteContent, data.Destination.ValueString())
   659→			}
   660→		}
   661→
   662→		errorMsg := diff.FormatDriftError(
   663→			data.ID.ValueString(),
   664→			data.Destination.ValueString(),
   665→			state.SourceHash.ValueString(),
   666→			remoteHash,
   667→			diffContent,
   668→		)
   669→
   670→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Remote file drift detected", errorMsg)
   671→		return
   672→	} else {
   673→		tflog.Debug(ctx, "No remote drift detected")
   674→	}
   675→
   676→	// Upload file.
   677→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Uploading file")
   678→	if err := client.UploadFile(ctx, data.Source.ValueString(), data.Destination.ValueString()); err != nil {
   679→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to upload file", err.Error())
   680→		return
   681→	}
   682→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "File uploaded successfully")
   683→
   684→	// Set ownership and permissions.
   685→	tflog.Debug(ctx, "Setting file attributes", map[string]interface{}{
   686→		"owner": data.Owner.ValueString(),
   687→		"group": data.Group.ValueString(),
   688→		"mode":  data.Mode.ValueString(),
   689→	})
   690→	if err := client.SetFileAttributes(
   691→		ctx,
   692→		data.Destination.ValueString(),
   693→		data.Owner.ValueString(),
   694→		data.Group.ValueString(),
   695→		data.Mode.ValueString(),
   696→	); err != nil {
   697→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("Failed to set file attributes", err.Error())
   698→		return
   699→	}
   700→
   701→	// Update computed values.
   702→	data.ID = types.StringValue(fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", data.Host.ValueString(), data.Destination.ValueString()))
   703→	data.SourceHash = types.StringValue(newHash)
   704→	data.Size = types.Int64Value(size)
   705→
   706→	tflog.Info(ctx, "File resource updated successfully", map[string]interface{}{
   707→		"id":   data.ID.ValueString(),
   708→		"size": size,
   709→	})
   710→
   711→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &data)...)
   712→}

   748→func (r *FileResource) ImportState(ctx context.Context, req resource.ImportStateRequest, resp *resource.ImportStateResponse) {
   749→	// Import format: "host:destination".
   750→	// Example: "192.168.1.100:/etc/myapp/config.json"
   751→	//
   752→	// After import, the user must update the config to set:.
   753→	// - source (required): path to the local source file
   754→	// - ssh_key_path or ssh_private_key (required): SSH credentials
   755→	//
   756→	// If import_syncs_local=true in the config, the remote file content will be
   757→	// written to the source path during the first Read after import.
   758→	//
   759→	// Then run `terraform apply` to sync state with the config.
   760→
   761→	id := req.ID
   762→	tflog.Info(ctx, "Importing file resource", map[string]interface{}{
   763→		"import_id": id,
   764→	})
   765→
   766→	// Parse the import ID - format is "host:destination".
   767→	// The destination is an absolute path, so we split on the first ":".
   768→	colonIdx := strings.Index(id, ":")
   769→	if colonIdx == -1 || colonIdx == 0 || colonIdx == len(id)-1 {
   770→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   771→			"Invalid Import ID",
   772→			fmt.Sprintf(
   773→				"Import ID must be in format 'host:destination' (e.g., '192.168.1.100:/etc/myapp/config.json').\n"+
   774→					"Got: %s", id,
   775→			),
   776→		)
   777→		return
   778→	}
   779→
   780→	host := id[:colonIdx]
   781→	destination := id[colonIdx+1:]
   782→
   783→	// Validate destination is an absolute path.
   784→	if !strings.HasPrefix(destination, "/") {
   785→		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
   786→			"Invalid Import ID",
   787→			fmt.Sprintf(
   788→				"Destination must be an absolute path starting with '/'.\n"+
   789→					"Got: %s", destination,
   790→			),
   791→		)
   792→		return
   793→	}
   794→
   795→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.SetAttribute(ctx, path.Root("id"), id)...)
   796→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.SetAttribute(ctx, path.Root("host"), host)...)
   797→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.SetAttribute(ctx, path.Root("destination"), destination)...)
   798→}

   800→// syncLocalFromRemote downloads the remote file content to the local source path.
   801→// This is called during Read when import_syncs_local=true and the local file
   802→// doesn't exist or differs from remote.
   803→func (r *FileResource) syncLocalFromRemote(ctx context.Context, data *FileResourceModel) error {
   804→	sourcePath := data.Source.ValueString()
   805→	if sourcePath == "" {
   806→		return fmt.Errorf("source path is not set - add 'source' attribute to your config")
   807→	}
   808→
   809→	tflog.Info(ctx, "Syncing local file from remote (import_syncs_local=true)", map[string]interface{}{
   810→		"source":      sourcePath,
   811→		"destination": data.Destination.ValueString(),
   812→	})
   813→
   814→	// Create SSH client.
   815→	client, err := r.createSSHClient(data)
   816→	if err != nil {
   817→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create SSH connection: %w", err)
   818→	}
   819→	defer r.releaseSSHClient(data, client)
   820→
   821→	// Check if remote file exists.
   822→	exists, err := client.FileExists(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString())
   823→	if err != nil {
   824→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check if remote file exists: %w", err)
   825→	}
   826→	if !exists {
   827→		return fmt.Errorf("remote file %s does not exist", data.Destination.ValueString())
   828→	}
   829→
   830→	// Read remote file content.
   831→	content, err := client.ReadFileContent(ctx, data.Destination.ValueString(), 0) // 0 = no limit
   832→	if err != nil {
   833→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to read remote file content: %w", err)
   834→	}
   835→
   836→	// Create parent directories if needed.
   837→	dir := filepath.Dir(sourcePath)
   838→	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0755); err != nil {
   839→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create parent directory %s: %w", dir, err)
   840→	}
   841→
   842→	// Write content to local file atomically (write to temp, then rename).
   843→	tmpPath := sourcePath + ".tmp"
   844→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpPath, content, 0644); err != nil {
   845→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write temporary file %s: %w", tmpPath, err)
   846→	}
   847→
   848→	if err := os.Rename(tmpPath, sourcePath); err != nil {
   849→		os.Remove(tmpPath) // Clean up temp file on error.
   850→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename temporary file to %s: %w", sourcePath, err)
   851→	}
   852→
   853→	tflog.Info(ctx, "Successfully synced local file from remote", map[string]interface{}{
   854→		"source": sourcePath,
   855→		"size":   len(content),
   856→	})
   857→
   858→	return nil
   859→}

   875→// createSSHClient creates or retrieves an SSH client (from pool if enabled).
   876→func (r *FileResource) createSSHClient(data *FileResourceModel) (gosftp.ClientInterface, error) {
   877→	config := r.getSSHConfig(data)
   878→
   879→	// Use connection pool if enabled.
   880→	if r.isPoolingEnabled() && r.providerConfig != nil && r.providerConfig.pool != nil {
   881→		return r.providerConfig.pool.GetOrCreate(config)
   882→	}
   883→
   884→	// Otherwise, create a new connection using the factory.
   885→	factory := r.sshClientFactory
   886→	if factory == nil {
   887→		factory = DefaultSSHClientFactory
   888→	}
   889→	client, err := factory(config)
   890→	if err != nil {
   891→		// Provide detailed error message for debugging SSH connection issues.
   892→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w (host=%s, port=%d, user=%s, insecure_ignore_host_key=%v, has_key=%v, has_password=%v)",
   893→			err,
   894→			config.Host,
   895→			config.Port,
   896→			config.User,
   897→			config.InsecureIgnoreHostKey,
   898→			config.KeyPath != "" || config.PrivateKey != "",
   899→			config.Password != "",
   900→		)
   901→	}
   902→	return client, nil
   903→}

   905→// releaseSSHClient releases a connection back to the pool (if pooling enabled).
   906→// If pooling is disabled, this closes the connection.
   907→func (r *FileResource) releaseSSHClient(data *FileResourceModel, client gosftp.ClientInterface) {
   908→	if r.isPoolingEnabled() && r.providerConfig != nil && r.providerConfig.pool != nil {
   909→		config := r.getSSHConfig(data)
   910→		r.providerConfig.pool.Release(config)
   911→		// Don't close - the pool manages the connection lifecycle.
   912→	} else {
   913→		// Not pooling - close the connection.
   914→		client.Close()
   915→	}
   916→}

   918→func hashFile(path string) (string, int64, error) {
   919→	f, err := os.Open(path)
   920→	if err != nil {
   921→		return "", 0, err
   922→	}
   923→	defer f.Close()
   924→
   925→	h := sha256.New()
   926→	size, err := io.Copy(h, f)
   927→	if err != nil {
   928→		return "", 0, err
   929→	}
   930→
   931→	return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)), size, nil
   932→}

   934→// sourceHashPlanModifier computes the source file hash during planning.
   935→// This allows Terraform to detect local file changes and trigger updates.
   936→type sourceHashPlanModifier struct{}

   938→func (m sourceHashPlanModifier) Description(_ context.Context) string {
   939→	return "Computes hash from current local source file to detect changes."
   940→}

   945→
   946→func (m sourceHashPlanModifier) PlanModifyString(ctx context.Context, req planmodifier.StringRequest, resp *planmodifier.StringResponse) {
   947→	// If resource is being destroyed, don't compute hash.
   948→	if req.Plan.Raw.IsNull() {
   949→		return
   950→	}
   951→
   952→	// Get the source path from the plan.
   953→	var sourcePath types.String
   954→	diags := req.Plan.GetAttribute(ctx, path.Root("source"), &sourcePath)
   955→	resp.Diagnostics.Append(diags...)
