# =============================================================================
# n8n LXC - Workflow Automation
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 502
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Plus traefik-route module for self-service routing.
# =============================================================================

module "n8n" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  # Identity
  name         = "n8n"
  container_id = 502

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores          = 2
  memory         = 2048
  swap           = 1024
  rootfs_size    = 8
  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

  # SSH
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Container options - unprivileged for security
  unprivileged = true
  template     = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox notes
  service_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}/"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.n8n}:5678/"
  }
  services = [
    { name = "n8n", port = 5678, info = "Web UI and API" }
  ]
  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Docker Deployment

**Compose file:** `/config/docker-compose.yml`
**Data volume:** `n8n_data`

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f n8n
```

**Restart n8n:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart n8n
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=n8n` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["n8n", "automation"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.n8n.container_id
  container_ip   = module.n8n.ip_address
  container_name = "n8n"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "SQLite backup"
      command = "cp /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite.backup"
      timeout = 60
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,n8n"
    ntfy_user     = "pbs-backup"
    ntfy_password = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["n8n"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["n8n"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "n8n"
  backend_url = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.n8n.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.n8n.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.n8n.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.n8n_route.internal_url
    direct   = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678/"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.n8n_route.remote_config_path
}

# =============================================================================
# n8n LXC - Workflow Automation
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 502
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Plus traefik-route module for self-service routing.
# =============================================================================

module "n8n" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  # Identity
  name         = "n8n"
  container_id = 502

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores          = 2
  memory         = 2048
  swap           = 1024
  rootfs_size    = 8
  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

  # SSH
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Container options - unprivileged for security
  unprivileged = true
  template     = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox notes
  service_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}/"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.n8n}:5678/"
  }
  services = [
    { name = "n8n", port = 5678, info = "Web UI and API" }
  ]
  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Docker Deployment

**Compose file:** `/config/docker-compose.yml`
**Data volume:** `n8n_data`

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f n8n
```

**Restart n8n:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart n8n
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=n8n` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["n8n", "automation"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.n8n.container_id
  container_ip   = module.n8n.ip_address
  container_name = "n8n"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "SQLite backup"
      command = "cp /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite.backup"
      timeout = 60
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,n8n"
    ntfy_user     = "pbs-backup"
    ntfy_password = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["n8n"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["n8n"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "n8n"
  backend_url = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.n8n.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.n8n.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.n8n.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.n8n_route.internal_url
    direct   = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678/"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.n8n_route.remote_config_path
}

# =============================================================================
# Docker LXC Module
# =============================================================================
# Opinionated module for deploying Docker-based applications in LXC containers.
# Uses lxc-base + filesync provider + remotedockercompose provider for a
# fully declarative deployment experience.
# =============================================================================

terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = {
      source  = "bpg/proxmox"
      version = "~> 0.69"
    }
    filesync = {
      source  = "darshan-rambhia/filesync"
      version = "~> 0.3"
    }
    ansible = {
      source  = "marshallford/ansible"
      version = "~> 0.9"
    }
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LXC Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "lxc" {
  source = "../lxc-base"

  name         = var.name
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network - dual-network architecture
  container_ip      = var.container_ip
  container_gateway = var.container_gateway
  lan_ip            = var.lan_ip
  lan_gateway       = var.lan_gateway

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Container type
  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
  template     = var.template

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key               = var.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Features
  enable_nesting = true
  enable_keyctl  = true
  enable_fuse    = false

  # GPU passthrough (AMD Radeon - /dev/kfd, /dev/dri)
  enable_gpu = var.enable_gpu

  # Mount points
  mount_points = var.mount_points

  # Proxmox notes
  description = var.enable_proxmox_notes ? templatefile("${path.module}/templates/notes.md.tftpl", {
    service_name = var.service_name != "" ? var.service_name : var.name
    description  = var.service_description
    urls         = var.service_urls
    services     = var.services
    ssh_host     = split("/", var.container_ip)[0]
    custom_notes = var.custom_notes
    managed_by   = true
  }) : ""

  # Tags
  tags = concat(["docker"], var.tags)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File Sync - Using filesync provider directly
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get list of all files in deploy directory, excluding specified patterns
locals {
  _all_deploy_files = var.deploy_dir != "" ? fileset(var.deploy_dir, "**") : []

  # Filter out files matching exclude patterns
  deploy_files = [
    for f in local._all_deploy_files : f
    if !anytrue([for pattern in var.exclude_patterns : can(regex(pattern, f))])
  ]
}

# Sync each file individually using filesync provider
resource "filesync_file" "config_files" {
  for_each = toset(local.deploy_files)

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${each.value}"
  destination = "${var.target_path}/${each.value}"
  host        = module.lxc.container_ip
  mode        = "0644"

  # SSH configuration - provider config is inherited but explicit for clarity
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.lxc]
}

# Set custom permissions for specific files
resource "filesync_file" "custom_permissions" {
  for_each = var.file_permissions

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${trimsuffix(trimprefix(each.key, var.target_path), "/")}"
  destination = each.key
  host        = module.lxc.container_ip
  mode        = each.value

  # SSH configuration
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [filesync_file.config_files]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Environment File (Secrets) - Synced BEFORE docker compose
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# When env_content is provided, write it to a temp file and sync to container.
# This ensures secrets are available before docker compose runs.

resource "local_sensitive_file" "env_file" {
  count = var.env_content != "" ? 1 : 0

  content         = var.env_content
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/${var.name}.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "env_file" {
  count = var.env_content != "" ? 1 : 0

  source      = local_sensitive_file.env_file[0].filename
  destination = "${var.target_path}/.env"
  host        = module.lxc.container_ip
  mode        = "0600"

  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [filesync_file.config_files]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Docker Compose Deployment via Ansible
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# After filesync completes, Ansible deploys and starts the containers

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "deploy_containers" {
  count = var.docker_compose_up ? 1 : 0

  depends_on = [
    filesync_file.config_files,
    filesync_file.custom_permissions,
    filesync_file.env_file  # Wait for .env to be synced before running docker compose
  ]

  triggers = {
    # Use 'run' key to trigger playbook re-run when config files or env change
    # See: https://registry.terraform.io/providers/marshallford/ansible/latest/docs/resources/navigator_run
    run = sha256(join(",", concat(
      [for f in local.deploy_files : filesha256("${var.deploy_dir}/${f}")],
      [sha256(var.env_content)]  # Include env_content in trigger hash
    )))
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false  # Run ansible directly on host
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = <<-EOT
    - name: Deploy Docker Compose for ${var.name}
      hosts: lxc
      gather_facts: no
      vars:
        config_dir: ${var.target_path}
        app_name: ${var.name}

      tasks:
        # =====================================================================
        # Verify Required Files
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Check docker-compose.yml exists
          ansible.builtin.stat:
            path: "{{ config_dir }}/docker-compose.yml"
          register: compose_file

        - name: Fail if docker-compose.yml missing
          ansible.builtin.fail:
            msg: "Required file missing: docker-compose.yml"
          when: not compose_file.stat.exists

        # =====================================================================
        # Pull Images & Start Containers
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Pull container images
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: docker compose -f {{ config_dir }}/docker-compose.yml pull
            chdir: "{{ config_dir }}"
          register: pull_result
          changed_when: "'Pulled' in pull_result.stdout or 'Downloaded' in pull_result.stdout"

        - name: Start containers
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: docker compose -f {{ config_dir }}/docker-compose.yml up -d --remove-orphans
            chdir: "{{ config_dir }}"
          register: up_result
          changed_when: "'Started' in up_result.stderr or 'Creating' in up_result.stderr or 'Created' in up_result.stderr"

        # =====================================================================
        # Health Checks
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Wait for containers to stabilize
          ansible.builtin.pause:
            seconds: 10

        - name: Get container status
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: docker compose -f {{ config_dir }}/docker-compose.yml ps --format json
            chdir: "{{ config_dir }}"
          register: ps_result
          changed_when: false

        - name: Verify all containers are running
          ansible.builtin.assert:
            that:
              - ps_result.stdout | length > 0
            fail_msg: "No containers found for {{ app_name }}"
            success_msg: "Containers deployed successfully for {{ app_name }}"
  EOT

  inventory = yamlencode({
    lxc = {
      hosts = {
        "${var.name}" = {
          ansible_host = module.lxc.container_ip
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - Loki + Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "Observability stack with Loki, Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana           = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus        = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager      = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma       = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy              = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_loki       = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100"
    direct_alloy_grpc = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317"
    direct_alloy_http = "http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Loki", port = 3100, info = "Log aggregation" },
    { name = "Alloy (gRPC)", port = 4317, info = "OTLP gRPC receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy (HTTP)", port = 4318, info = "OTLP HTTP receiver" },
    { name = "Alloy UI", port = 12345, info = "Alloy debug UI" },
    { name = "Prometheus", port = 9090, info = "Metrics storage and alerting" },
    { name = "Grafana", port = 3000, info = "Dashboards and visualization" },
    { name = "Alertmanager", port = 9093, info = "Alert routing" },
    { name = "Uptime Kuma", port = 3001, info = "HTTP monitoring and status page" },
    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Alloy OTLP Endpoints (for Proxmox/Immich)

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317
**OTLP HTTP:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4318

Configure Proxmox metrics server:
```bash
pvesh create /cluster/metrics/server \
  --id homelab-alloy \
  --type opentelemetry \
  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \
  --port 4317 \
  --proto grpc
```

## Loki Endpoint (for Alloy sidecars)

**Loki URL:** http://${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:3100

## Grafana

Default login: admin / (password in 1Password)

## ntfy Topics

- `homelab-alerts` - Prometheus alerts
- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

Subscribe via mobile app or web UI.

## Quick Commands

```bash
# View Alloy logs
docker logs -f alloy

# View Loki logs
docker logs -f loki

# Query logs via Loki API
curl -s "http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/labels" | jq

# Reload Prometheus config
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload

# Test ntfy notification
curl -d "Test notification" http://localhost:8080/homelab-alerts
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=monitoring` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["monitoring", "loki", "alloy", "prometheus", "grafana"]

  # Pass env content to module - synced BEFORE docker compose runs
  env_content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    grafana_admin_password = local.op.grafana_admin_password
    uptime_kuma_username   = local.op.uptime_kuma_username
    uptime_kuma_password   = local.op.uptime_kuma_password
    discord_webhook_url    = local.op.discord_webhook_url
    # Grafana OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
    grafana_oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.grafana.client_id
    grafana_oauth_client_secret = random_password.grafana_oidc_secret.result
    grafana_oauth_auth_url      = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/authorize/"
    grafana_oauth_token_url     = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/token/"
    grafana_oauth_api_url       = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/userinfo/"
    grafana_oauth_signout_url   = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/grafana/end-session/"
    # ntfy credentials for Alertmanager
    ntfy_alertmanager_password = local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password
    # ntfy credentials for Discord forwarder
    ntfy_discord_forwarder_password = local.op.ntfy_discord_forwarder_password
  })
}

# Note: .env file is now handled by the docker-lxc module via env_content
# This ensures the .env is synced BEFORE docker compose runs

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ntfy User Provisioning (Ansible)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provisions ntfy users and ACL after container deployment

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "ntfy_provision" {
  triggers = {
    container_id = module.monitoring.container_id
    container_ip = module.monitoring.ip_address
    # Re-run if credentials change
    credentials_hash = sha256(join(",", [
      local.op.ntfy_admin_password,
      local.op.ntfy_darshan_password,
      local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password,
      local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password,
      local.op.ntfy_n8n_password,
      local.op.ntfy_uptime_kuma_password,
      local.op.ntfy_discord_forwarder_password,
    ]))
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/ntfy/provision-users.yml.tpl", {
    ntfy_admin_user                 = local.op.ntfy_admin_user
    ntfy_admin_password             = local.op.ntfy_admin_password
    ntfy_darshan_password           = local.op.ntfy_darshan_password
    ntfy_alertmanager_password      = local.op.ntfy_alertmanager_password
    ntfy_pbs_backup_password        = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
    ntfy_n8n_password               = local.op.ntfy_n8n_password
    ntfy_uptime_kuma_password       = local.op.ntfy_uptime_kuma_password
    ntfy_discord_forwarder_password = local.op.ntfy_discord_forwarder_password
  })

  inventory = yamlencode({
    monitoring = {
      hosts = {
        "monitoring" = {
          ansible_host = module.monitoring.ip_address
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "grafana_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "grafana"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "grafana.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "prometheus_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "prometheus"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9090"

  internal_domain = "prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "alertmanager_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "alertmanager"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:9093"

  internal_domain = "alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "uptime_kuma_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "status"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3001"

  internal_domain = "status.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

module "ntfy_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "ntfy"
  backend_url = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:8080"

  internal_domain = "ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # ntfy has its own ACL-based authentication - no Authentik middleware
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.monitoring.container_id
  container_ip   = module.monitoring.ip_address
  container_name = "monitoring"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,monitoring"
    ntfy_user     = "pbs-backup"
    ntfy_password = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["monitoring"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  depends_on = [module.monitoring]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.monitoring.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.monitoring.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.monitoring.ssh_command
}

output "alloy_endpoints" {
  value = {
    grpc = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4317"
    http = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:4318"
  }
}

output "loki_url" {
  value = "http://${module.monitoring.ip_address}:3100"
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.internal_url
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.internal_url
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.internal_url
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.internal_url
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    grafana      = module.grafana_route.remote_config_path
    prometheus   = module.prometheus_route.remote_config_path
    alertmanager = module.alertmanager_route.remote_config_path
    uptime_kuma  = module.uptime_kuma_route.remote_config_path
    ntfy         = module.ntfy_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

   728→          "jsCode": "const allContainers = [];\nconst seenImages = new Set();\nconst lxcItems = $('Split LXCs').all();\nconst sshItems = $input.all();\n\nfunction parseImage(image) {\n  let registry = 'docker.io', repository = image, tag = 'latest';\n  const tagMatch = repository.match(/^(.+):([^:]+)$/);\n  if (tagMatch) { repository = tagMatch[1]; tag = tagMatch[2]; }\n  if (repository.includes('/')) {\n    const firstPart = repository.split('/')[0];\n    if (firstPart.includes('.') || firstPart.includes(':')) {\n      registry = firstPart;\n      repository = repository.substring(firstPart.length + 1);\n    }\n  }\n  if (!repository.includes('/') && registry === 'docker.io') repository = 'library/' + repository;\n  return { registry, repository, current_tag: tag };\n}\n\nfor (let i = 0; i < sshItems.length; i++) {\n  const stdout = sshItems[i].json.stdout || '';\n  const lxcId = lxcItems[i]?.json?.id || 'unknown';\n  const lxcName = lxcItems[i]?.json?.name || 'unknown';\n  \n  for (const line of stdout.split('\\n')) {\n    if (!line.trim() || line === '{}') continue;\n    try {\n      const container = JSON.parse(line);\n      const name = container.Names || '', image = container.Image || '';\n      if (name && image && !seenImages.has(image)) {\n        seenImages.add(image);\n        allContainers.push({ json: { lxcId, lxcName, containerName: name, image, skip: false, ...parseImage(image) } });\n      }\n    } catch (e) {}\n  }\n}\n\nreturn allContainers.length ? allContainers : [{ json: { skip: true, skip_reason: 'No containers found' } }];"

# AI Agent node

An [AI agent](/glossary.md#ai-agent) is an autonomous system that receives data, makes rational decisions, and acts within its environment to achieve specific goals. The AI agent's environment is everything the agent can access that isn't the agent itself. This agent uses external [tools](/glossary.md#ai-tool) and APIs to perform actions and retrieve information. It can understand the capabilities of different tools and determine which tool to use depending on the task. 

/// note | Connect a tool
You must connect at least one tool [sub-node](/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/sub-nodes/index.md) to an AI Agent node.
///

/// note | Agent type
Prior to version 1.82.0, the AI Agent had a setting for working as different agent types. This has now been removed and all AI Agent nodes work as a `Tools Agent` which was the recommended and most frequently used setting. If you're working with older versions of the AI Agent in workflows or templates, as long as they were set to 'Tools Agent', they should continue to behave as intended with the updated node.
///

# Ollama Chat Model node

The Ollama Chat Model node allows you use local Llama 2 models with conversational [agents](/glossary.md#ai-agent).

On this page, you'll find the node parameters for the Ollama Chat Model node, and links to more resources.

/// note | Credentials
You can find authentication information for this node [here](/integrations/builtin/credentials/ollama.md).
///

--8<-- "_snippets/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/sub-node-expression-resolution.md"

## Node parameters

* **Model**: Select the model that generates the completion. Choose from:
	* **Llama2**
	* **Llama2 13B**
	* **Llama2 70B**
	* **Llama2 Uncensored**

Refer to the Ollama [Models Library documentation](https://ollama.com/library){:target=_blank .external-link} for more information about available models.

## Node options

* **Sampling Temperature**: Use this option to control the randomness of the sampling process. A higher temperature creates more diverse sampling, but increases the risk of hallucinations.
* **Top K**: Enter the number of token choices the model uses to generate the next token.
* **Top P**: Use this option to set the probability the completion should use. Use a lower value to ignore less probable options.

This template is ideal for creators, content marketers, social media managers, and AI enthusiasts who want to automate the production of short-form, visually captivating videos for platforms like TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels — all without manual editing or publishing.

What problem is this workflow solving?

Creating engaging videos requires:

      "name": "Fully Automated AI Video Generation & Multi-Platform Publishing",
      "description": "Description

This comprehensive n8n automation template orchestrates a complete end-to-end workflow for generating engaging short-form Point-of-View (POV) style videos using multiple AI services and automatically publishing them across major social media platforms. It takes ideas from a Google Sheet and transforms them into finished videos with captions, voiceovers, and platform-specific descriptions, ready for distribution.

Who Is This For?

Content Creators & Agencies:** Mass-produce unique short-form video content for various clients or channels with minimal manual effort.
Digital Marketers:** Automate video content pipelines to boost online presence and engagement across multiple platforms simultaneously.
Social Media Managers:** Schedule and distribute consistent video content efficiently without juggling multiple tools and manual uploads.
Businesses:** Leverage AI to create branded video content for marketing, reducing production time and costs.

What Problem Does This Workflow Solve?

Creating and distributing high-quality short-form video content consistently across multiple social networks is incredibly time-consuming and resource-intensive. This workflow tackles these challenges by:

Automating Idea-to-Video Pipeline:** Generates video concepts, image prompts, scripts, images, video clips, and voiceovers using AI.
Streamlining Video Assembly:** Automatically combines generated assets into a final video using a template.
Generating Platform-Optimized Descriptions:** Creates relevant descriptions for posts by transcribing the final video audio.
Automating Multi-Platform Publishing:** Uploads the final video and description to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, and LinkedIn simultaneously.
Reducing Manual Workload:** Drastically cuts down the time and effort required for video production and distribution.
Centralized Tracking:** Updates a Google Sheet with results, costs, and status for easy monitoring.

How It Works

Trigger & Input: Runs on a daily schedule (configurable) and fetches new video ideas from a designated Google Sheet.
AI Content Generation:
    Uses OpenAI to generate video captions and image prompts based on the idea.
    Uses PiAPI (Flux) to generate images from prompts.
    Uses PiAPI (Kling) to generate video clips from the images (Image-to-Video).
    Uses OpenAI to generate a voiceover script based on the captions.
    Uses ElevenLabs to generate voiceover audio from the script and uploads it to Google Drive.
Video Assembly: Combines the generated video clips, captions, and voiceover audio using a Creatomate template to render the final video.
Description Generation: Uploads the final video to Google Drive, extracts the audio using OpenAI (Whisper), and generates a social media description using OpenAI (GPT).
Multi-Platform Distribution: Uses upload-post.com to upload the final video and generated description to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, and LinkedIn.
Tracking & Notification: Updates the original Google Sheet row with output details (video link, costs, tokens used) and sends a completion notification via Discord.

Setup

Accounts & API Keys: Obtain accounts and generate API keys/credentials for:
    n8n
    Google Cloud Platform (for Google Sheets & Google Drive APIs + OAuth Credentials)
    OpenAI
    PiAPI
    ElevenLabs
    Creatomate
    upload-post.com
    Discord (Webhook URL)
Google Sheet: Make a copy of the provided Google Sheet Template and connect it in the Load Google Sheet node.
Creatomate Template: Set up a video template in Creatomate (use the provided JSON source code as a base) and note its Template ID.
Configure Nodes:
    Enter all API Keys/Credentials in the Set API Keys node and other relevant credential sections (Google nodes, upload-post nodes, etc.).
    Configure Google Drive nodes (Folder IDs, Permissions).
    Configure the upload-post.com nodes with your user identifier and necessary platform details (e.g., Facebook Page ID).
    Customize AI prompts within the OpenAI nodes (Generate Video Captions, Generate Image Prompts, Generate Script, Generate Description...) if desired.
    Set the Discord Webhook URL in the Notify me on Discord node.
Enable Google APIs: Ensure Google Drive API and Google Sheets API are enabled in your Google Cloud Project.

Requirements

Accounts:** n8n, Google (Sheets, Drive, Cloud Platform), OpenAI, PiAPI, ElevenLabs, Creatomate, The social media api Upload-Post, Discord.
API Keys & Credentials:** API Keys for OpenAI, PiAPI, ElevenLabs, Creatomate, upload-post.com. Google Cloud OAuth 2.0 Credentials. Discord Webhook URL.
Templates:** A configured Google Sheet based on the template, a configured Creatomate video template.
(Potentially) Paid Plans:** Some services (OpenAI, PiAPI, Creatomate, upload-post.com) may require paid plans depending on usage volume after free trials/credits are exhausted.

Use this template to build a powerful, automated video content factory, scaling your production and distribution efforts across the social media landscape.",

      "description": "This workflow allows users to generate AI videos using Google Veo3, save them to Google Drive, generate optimized YouTube titles with GPT-4o, and automatically upload them to YouTube with Upload-Post. The entire process is triggered from a Google Sheet that acts as the central interface for input and output.

IT automates video creation, uploading, and tracking, ensuring seamless integration between Google Sheets, Google Drive, Google Veo3, and YouTube.

Benefits of this Workflow

💡 No Code Interface**: Trigger and control the video production pipeline from a simple Google Sheet.
⚙️ Full Automation**: Once set up, the entire video generation and publishing process runs hands-free.
🧠 AI-Powered Creativity**:

  Generates engaging YouTube titles using GPT-4o.
  Leverages advanced generative video AI from Google Veo3.
📁 Cloud Storage & Backup**: Stores all generated videos on Google Drive for safekeeping.
📈 YouTube Ready**: Automatically uploads to YouTube with correct metadata, saving time and boosting visibility.
🧪 Scalable**: Designed to process multiple video prompts by looping through new entries in Google Sheets.
🔒 API-First**: Utilizes secure API-based communication for all services.

How It Works  
Trigger: The workflow can be started manually ("When clicking ‘Test workflow’") or scheduled ("Schedule Trigger") to run at regular intervals (e.g., every 5 minutes).  
Fetch Data: The "Get new video" node retrieves unfilled video requests from a Google Sheet (rows where the "VIDEO" column is empty).  
Video Creation:  
   The "Set data" node formats the prompt and duration from the Google Sheet.  
   The "Create Video" node sends a request to the Fal.run API (Google Veo3) to generate a video based on the prompt.  
Status Check:  
   The "Wait 60 sec." node pauses execution for 60 seconds.  
   The "Get status" node checks the video generation status. If the status is "COMPLETED," the workflow proceeds; otherwise, it waits again.  
Video Processing:  
   The "Get Url Video" node fetches the video URL.  
   The "Generate title" node uses OpenAI (GPT-4.1) to create an SEO-optimized YouTube title.  
   The "Get File Video" node downloads the video file.  
Upload & Update:  
   The "Upload Video" node saves the video to Google Drive.  
   The "HTTP Request" node uploads the video to YouTube via the Upload-Post API.  
   The "Update Youtube URL" and "Update result" nodes update the Google Sheet with the video URL and YouTube link.  

Set Up Steps  
Google Sheet Setup:  
   Create a Google Sheet with columns: PROMPT, DURATION, VIDEO, and YOUTUBE_URL.  
   Share the Sheet link in the "Get new video" node.  

API Keys:  
   Obtain a Fal.run API key (for Veo3) and set it in the "Create Video" node (Header: Authorization: Key YOURAPIKEY).  
   Get an Upload-Post API key (for YouTube uploads) and configure the "HTTP Request" node (Header: Authorization: Apikey YOUR_API_KEY).  

YouTube Upload Configuration:  
   Replace YOUR_USERNAME in the "HTTP Request" node with your Upload-Post profile name.  

Schedule Trigger:  
   Configure the "Schedule Trigger" node to run periodically (e.g., every 5 minutes).

      "name": "Build Your First AI Agent",
      "description": "How it works

This template launches your very first AI Agent —an AI-powered chatbot that can do more than just talk— it can take action using tools.

The Chat Interface:** A Chat Trigger node provides a simple, clean interface for you to talk to your agent.

The Tools:** It comes pre-equipped with two tools to demonstrate its capabilities:

      "name": "RAG Chatbot for Company Documents using Google Drive and Gemini",
      "description": "This workflow implements a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot that answers employee questions based on company documents stored in Google Drive. It automatically indexes new or updated documents in a Pinecone vector database, allowing the chatbot to provide accurate and up-to-date information. The workflow uses Google's Gemini AI for both embeddings and response generation.

How it works
The workflow uses two Google Drive Trigger nodes: one for detecting new files added to a specified Google Drive folder, and another for detecting file updates in that same folder.
Automated Indexing: When a new or updated document is detected
The Google Drive node downloads the file.
The Default Data Loader node loads the document content.
The Recursive Character Text Splitter node breaks the document into smaller text chunks.
The Embeddings Google Gemini node generates embeddings for each text chunk using the text-embedding-004 model.
The Pinecone Vector Store node indexes the text chunks and their embeddings in a specified Pinecone index.
7.The Chat Trigger node receives user questions through a chat interface. The user's question is passed to an AI Agent node.
The AI Agent node uses a Vector Store Tool node, linked to a Pinecone Vector Store node in query mode, to retrieve relevant text chunks from Pinecone based on the user's question.
The AI Agent sends the retrieved information and the user's question to the Google Gemini Chat Model (gemini-pro).
The Google Gemini Chat Model generates a comprehensive and informative answer based on the retrieved documents.
A Window Buffer Memory node connected to the AI Agent provides short-term memory, allowing for more natural and context-aware conversations.

Set up steps

Google Cloud Project and Vertex AI API:
Create a Google Cloud project.
Enable the Vertex AI API for your project.
Google AI API Key:
Obtain a Google AI API key from Google AI Studio.
Pinecone Account:
Create a free account on the Pinecone website.
Obtain your API key from your Pinecone dashboard.
Create an index named company-files in your Pinecone project.
Google Drive:
Create a dedicated folder in your Google Drive where company documents will be stored.
Credentials in n8n: Configure credentials in your n8n environment for:
Google Drive OAuth2
Google Gemini(PaLM) Api (using your Google AI API key)
Pinecone API (using your Pinecone API key)
Import the Workflow:
Import this workflow into your n8n instance.
Configure the Workflow:
Update both Google Drive Trigger nodes to watch the specific folder you created in your Google Drive.
Configure the Pinecone Vector Store nodes to use your company-files index.",

Businesses:** Leverage AI to create branded video content for marketing, reducing production time and costs.

What Problem Does This Workflow Solve?

Creating and distributing high-quality short-form video content consistently across multiple social networks is incredibly time-consuming and resource-intensive. This workflow tackles these challenges by:

Automating Idea-to-Video Pipeline:** Generates video concepts, image prompts, scripts, images, video clips, and voiceovers using AI.
Streamlining Video Assembly:** Automatically combines generated assets into a final video using a template.
Generating Platform-Optimized Descriptions:** Creates relevant descriptions for posts by transcribing the final video audio.
Automating Multi-Platform Publishing:** Uploads the final video and description to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, and LinkedIn simultaneously.
Reducing Manual Workload:** Drastically cuts down the time and effort required for video production and distribution.
Centralized Tracking:** Updates a Google Sheet with results, costs, and status for easy monitoring.

How It Works

Trigger & Input: Runs on a daily schedule (configurable) and fetches new video ideas from a designated Google Sheet.
AI Content Generation:
    Uses OpenAI to generate video captions and image prompts based on the idea.
    Uses PiAPI (Flux) to generate images from prompts.
    Uses PiAPI (Kling) to generate video clips from the images (Image-to-Video).
    Uses OpenAI to generate a voiceover script based on the captions.
    Uses ElevenLabs to generate voiceover audio from the script and uploads it to Google Drive.
Video Assembly: Combines the generated video clips, captions, and voiceover audio using a Creatomate template to render the final video.
Description Generation: Uploads the final video to Google Drive, extracts the audio using OpenAI (Whisper), and generates a social media description using OpenAI (GPT).
Multi-Platform Distribution: Uses upload-post.com to upload the final video and generated description to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, and LinkedIn.
Tracking & Notification: Updates the original Google Sheet row with output details (video link, costs, tokens used) and sends a completion notification via Discord.

Setup

    n8n
    Google Cloud Platform (for Google Sheets & Google Drive APIs + OAuth Credentials)
    OpenAI
    PiAPI
    ElevenLabs
    Creatomate
    upload-post.com
    Discord (Webhook URL)
Google Sheet: Make a copy of the provided Google Sheet Template and connect it in the Load Google Sheet node.
Creatomate Template: Set up a video template in Creatomate (use the provided JSON source code as a base) and note its Template ID.
Configure Nodes:
    Enter all API Keys/Credentials in the Set API Keys node and other relevant credential sections (Google nodes, upload-post nodes, etc.).
    Configure Google Drive nodes (Folder IDs, Permissions).
    Configure the upload-post.com nodes with your user identifier and necessary platform details (e.g., Facebook Page ID).
    Customize AI prompts within the OpenAI nodes (Generate Video Captions, Generate Image Prompts, Generate Script, Generate Description...) if desired.
    Set the Discord Webhook URL in the Notify me on Discord node.
Enable Google APIs: Ensure Google Drive API and Google Sheets API are enabled in your Google Cloud Project.

Requirements

Accounts:** n8n, Google (Sheets, Drive, Cloud Platform), OpenAI, PiAPI, ElevenLabs, Creatomate, The social media api Upload-Post, Discord.
API Keys & Credentials:** API Keys for OpenAI, PiAPI, ElevenLabs, Creatomate, upload-post.com. Google Cloud OAuth 2.0 Credentials. Discord Webhook URL.
Templates:** A configured Google Sheet based on the template, a configured Creatomate video template.
(Potentially) Paid Plans:** Some services (OpenAI, PiAPI, Creatomate, upload-post.com) may require paid plans depending on usage volume after free trials/credits are exhausted.

      "description": "This workflow allows users to generate AI videos using Google Veo3, save them to Google Drive, generate optimized YouTube titles with GPT-4o, and automatically upload them to YouTube with Upload-Post. The entire process is triggered from a Google Sheet that acts as the central interface for input and output.

IT automates video creation, uploading, and tracking, ensuring seamless integration between Google Sheets, Google Drive, Google Veo3, and YouTube.

Benefits of this Workflow

💡 No Code Interface**: Trigger and control the video production pipeline from a simple Google Sheet.
⚙️ Full Automation**: Once set up, the entire video generation and publishing process runs hands-free.
🧠 AI-Powered Creativity**:

  Generates engaging YouTube titles using GPT-4o.
  Leverages advanced generative video AI from Google Veo3.
📁 Cloud Storage & Backup**: Stores all generated videos on Google Drive for safekeeping.
📈 YouTube Ready**: Automatically uploads to YouTube with correct metadata, saving time and boosting visibility.
🧪 Scalable**: Designed to process multiple video prompts by looping through new entries in Google Sheets.
🔒 API-First**: Utilizes secure API-based communication for all services.

How It Works  
Trigger: The workflow can be started manually ("When clicking ‘Test workflow’") or scheduled ("Schedule Trigger") to run at regular intervals (e.g., every 5 minutes).  
Fetch Data: The "Get new video" node retrieves unfilled video requests from a Google Sheet (rows where the "VIDEO" column is empty).  
Video Creation:  
   The "Set data" node formats the prompt and duration from the Google Sheet.  
   The "Create Video" node sends a request to the Fal.run API (Google Veo3) to generate a video based on the prompt.  
Status Check:  
   The "Wait 60 sec." node pauses execution for 60 seconds.  
   The "Get status" node checks the video generation status. If the status is "COMPLETED," the workflow proceeds; otherwise, it waits again.  
Video Processing:  
   The "Get Url Video" node fetches the video URL.  
   The "Generate title" node uses OpenAI (GPT-4.1) to create an SEO-optimized YouTube title.  
   The "Get File Video" node downloads the video file.  
Upload & Update:  
   The "Upload Video" node saves the video to Google Drive.  
   The "HTTP Request" node uploads the video to YouTube via the Upload-Post API.  
   The "Update Youtube URL" and "Update result" nodes update the Google Sheet with the video URL and YouTube link.  

Set Up Steps  
Google Sheet Setup:  
   Create a Google Sheet with columns: PROMPT, DURATION, VIDEO, and YOUTUBE_URL.  
   Share the Sheet link in the "Get new video" node.  

API Keys:  
   Obtain a Fal.run API key (for Veo3) and set it in the "Create Video" node (Header: Authorization: Key YOURAPIKEY).  
   Get an Upload-Post API key (for YouTube uploads) and configure the "HTTP Request" node (Header: Authorization: Apikey YOUR_API_KEY).  

YouTube Upload Configuration:  
   Replace YOUR_USERNAME in the "HTTP Request" node with your Upload-Post profile name.  

Schedule Trigger:  
   Configure the "Schedule Trigger" node to run periodically (e.g., every 5 minutes).

      "name": "RAG Chatbot for Company Documents using Google Drive and Gemini",
      "description": "This workflow implements a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot that answers employee questions based on company documents stored in Google Drive. It automatically indexes new or updated documents in a Pinecone vector database, allowing the chatbot to provide accurate and up-to-date information. The workflow uses Google's Gemini AI for both embeddings and response generation.

How it works
The workflow uses two Google Drive Trigger nodes: one for detecting new files added to a specified Google Drive folder, and another for detecting file updates in that same folder.
Automated Indexing: When a new or updated document is detected
The Google Drive node downloads the file.
The Default Data Loader node loads the document content.
The Recursive Character Text Splitter node breaks the document into smaller text chunks.
The Embeddings Google Gemini node generates embeddings for each text chunk using the text-embedding-004 model.
The Pinecone Vector Store node indexes the text chunks and their embeddings in a specified Pinecone index.
7.The Chat Trigger node receives user questions through a chat interface. The user's question is passed to an AI Agent node.
The AI Agent node uses a Vector Store Tool node, linked to a Pinecone Vector Store node in query mode, to retrieve relevant text chunks from Pinecone based on the user's question.
The AI Agent sends the retrieved information and the user's question to the Google Gemini Chat Model (gemini-pro).
The Google Gemini Chat Model generates a comprehensive and informative answer based on the retrieved documents.
A Window Buffer Memory node connected to the AI Agent provides short-term memory, allowing for more natural and context-aware conversations.

Set up steps

Google Cloud Project and Vertex AI API:
Create a Google Cloud project.
Enable the Vertex AI API for your project.
Google AI API Key:
Obtain a Google AI API key from Google AI Studio.
Pinecone Account:
Create a free account on the Pinecone website.
Obtain your API key from your Pinecone dashboard.
Create an index named company-files in your Pinecone project.
Google Drive:
Create a dedicated folder in your Google Drive where company documents will be stored.
Credentials in n8n: Configure credentials in your n8n environment for:
Google Drive OAuth2
Google Gemini(PaLM) Api (using your Google AI API key)
Pinecone API (using your Pinecone API key)
Import the Workflow:
Import this workflow into your n8n instance.
Configure the Workflow:
Update both Google Drive Trigger nodes to watch the specific folder you created in your Google Drive.
Configure the Pinecone Vector Store nodes to use your company-files index.",

Update the Creatomate template to reflect your visual branding
Configure notification preferences in Discord to manage your workflow

# =============================================================================
# OpenWebUI LXC - AI Chat Interface with llama.cpp
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 501
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Features Vulkan GPU acceleration for llama.cpp (AMD Radeon 890M gfx1150).
#
# Benchmarked performance (Vulkan vs ROCm vs CPU):
#   - Vulkan: ~800 tok/s prompt, ~40 tok/s generation (WINNER)
#   - ROCm:   ~30 tok/s prompt,  ~29 tok/s generation
#   - CPU:    ~28 tok/s prompt,  ~28 tok/s generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Mount points - LLM models on ZFS tank for unlimited storage
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/llm-models"
      volume = "/tank/llm-models"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Make download script executable
  file_permissions = {
    "/config/download-model.sh" = "0755"
  }

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with llama.cpp backend (Vulkan GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenWebUI - AI Chat Interface
  # ==========================================================================
  openwebui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.6.43
    container_name: openwebui
    environment:
      # Use llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible API instead of Ollama
      - OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://llama-server:8080/v1
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed
      - ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
      - WEBUI_NAME=Homelab AI
      - ENABLE_SIGNUP=false  # Security: Disable public signup
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=llama-3.2-3b-instruct
      # Session secret key (must be persistent)
      - WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=${WEBUI_SECRET_KEY}
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
      - ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP=true
      - OAUTH_MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL=true
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=${OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=${OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - OPENID_PROVIDER_URL=${OPENID_PROVIDER_URL}
      - OAUTH_PROVIDER_NAME=Authentik
      - OAUTH_SCOPES=openid email profile
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./openwebui:/app/backend/data
    depends_on:
      llama-server:
        condition: service_healthy
    # DNS settings for external resolution
    dns:
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 1.1.1.1
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 20480m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 8192m
          cpus: '4.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # llama.cpp Server - LLM Backend (Vulkan GPU Accelerated)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Using Vulkan backend for AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) - provides best
  # performance vs ROCm/CPU. Benchmarked at ~40 tok/s generation,
  # ~800 tok/s prompt processing.
  # ==========================================================================
  llama-server:
    image: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan
    container_name: llama-server
    environment:
      # Router mode: scans /models directory for all GGUF files
      # Models are loaded on-demand when requested via API
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_DIR=/models
      # Max models to load simultaneously (default: 4)
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_MAX=2
      # Autoload models when requested
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_AUTOLOAD=true
      - LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE=8192
      - LLAMA_ARG_N_GPU_LAYERS=99
      - LLAMA_ARG_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - LLAMA_ARG_PORT=8080
      # Flash attention for better memory efficiency
      - LLAMA_ARG_FLASH_ATTN=1
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Models stored on ZFS tank (/tank/llm-models) for unlimited storage
      - /llm-models:/models
    # Vulkan GPU passthrough (simpler than ROCm - no /dev/kfd needed)
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 16384m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/health > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # n8n - Workflow Automation
  # ==========================================================================
  n8n:
    container_name: n8n
    image: n8nio/n8n:2.1.4
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "5678:5678"
    environment:
      - N8N_HOST=${N8N_HOST:-n8n.homelab.rambtech.dev}
      - N8N_PORT=5678
      - N8N_PROTOCOL=https
      - WEBHOOK_URL=https://${N8N_HOST:-n8n.homelab.rambtech.dev}/
      - GENERIC_TIMEZONE=America/Los_Angeles
      - TZ=America/Los_Angeles
      # SSO via Authentik forwardAuth (community edition workaround)
      - EXTERNAL_HOOK_FILES=/home/node/.n8n/hooks.js
      - N8N_FORWARD_AUTH_HEADER=x-authentik-email
      - AUTHENTIK_LOGOUT_URL=https://auth.rambtech.dev/flows/-/default/invalidation/
      # Allow node-fetch for Code nodes (used by Docker Update Checker workflow)
      - NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=node-fetch
    volumes:
      - n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n
      - ./hooks.js:/home/node/.n8n/hooks.js:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:5678/healthz || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Discord Bot - Forwards messages to n8n webhook
  # ==========================================================================
  discord-bot:
    container_name: discord-bot
    build: ./discord-bot
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN}
      - N8N_WEBHOOK_URL=http://n8n:5678/webhook/discord-updates
      # Optional: Restrict to specific channel or users
      # - ALLOWED_CHANNEL_ID=${DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID:-}
      # - ALLOWED_USER_IDS=${DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS:-}
    depends_on:
      n8n:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'

volumes:
  n8n_data:

You're right. For Discord bots, you need to add a redirect URL in the OAuth2 settings. Let me clarify the OAuth2 setup:

For a **bot-only** application (which is what we're building), you actually don't need a redirect URL. The redirect URL is only required if you're using OAuth2 for user authentication (like "Login with Discord").

For inviting a bot to a server, you use the **URL Generator** which creates a direct invite link. Here's the corrected process:

## Create Discord Bot (Updated Steps)

1. Go to https://discord.com/developers/applications
2. Click **New Application** → name it (e.g., "Homelab Assistant")
3. Go to **Bot** section in the left sidebar
4. Click **Reset Token** to generate a bot token → **Copy and save it**
5. Enable these **Privileged Gateway Intents**:
   - ✅ Message Content Intent
   - ✅ Server Members Intent (optional)
6. Go to **OAuth2** → **URL Generator**:
   - Under **Scopes**: select `bot`
   - Under **Bot Permissions**: select:
     - `Send Messages`
     - `Read Message History`  
     - `View Channels`
7. Copy the **Generated URL** at the bottom
8. Open that URL in your browser to invite the bot to your server

The redirect URL field in OAuth2 → General is only needed if you were building a web app that lets users "Login with Discord" - which we're not doing here. The bot uses the token directly to connect via WebSocket.

# =============================================================================
# n8n LXC - Workflow Automation
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 502
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Plus traefik-route module for self-service routing.
# =============================================================================

module "n8n" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  # Identity
  name         = "n8n"
  container_id = 502

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores          = 2
  memory         = 2048
  swap           = 1024
  rootfs_size    = 8
  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

  # Environment variables (synced BEFORE docker compose runs)
  env_content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    discord_bot_token = try(local.op.discord_bot_token, "PLACEHOLDER_CREATE_1PASSWORD_ITEM")
  })

  # Exclude .env files from filesync (handled by env_content)
  exclude_patterns = ["\\.env.*"]

  # SSH
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Container options - unprivileged for security
  unprivileged = true
  template     = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox notes
  service_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}/"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.n8n}:5678/"
  }
  services = [
    { name = "n8n", port = 5678, info = "Web UI and API" }
  ]
  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Docker Deployment

**Compose file:** `/config/docker-compose.yml`
**Data volume:** `n8n_data`

## Services

| Container | Purpose |
| --------- | ------- |
| n8n | Workflow automation platform |
| discord-bot | Forwards Discord messages to n8n webhooks |

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f n8n
cd /config && docker compose logs -f discord-bot
```

**Restart services:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart n8n
cd /config && docker compose restart discord-bot
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.n8n.container_id
  container_ip   = module.n8n.ip_address
  container_name = "n8n"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "SQLite backup"
      command = "cp /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite.backup"
      timeout = 60
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,n8n"
    ntfy_user     = "pbs-backup"
    ntfy_password = local.op.ntfy_pbs_backup_password
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["n8n"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["n8n"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "n8n"
  backend_url = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - authentik provides SSO authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authentik"]

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.n8n.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.n8n.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.n8n.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {

    internal = module.n8n_route.internal_url
    direct   = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678/"
  }
}

}

content.content:
1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→# n8n Workflow Sync Script
     3→# Usage: n8n-workflows.sh <command> [options]
     4→#
     5→# Commands:
     6→#   list              - List all workflows in n8n
     7→#   pull [--id=xxx]   - Pull workflows from n8n to local files
     8→#   push [--id=xxx]   - Push local workflows to n8n
     9→#   diff --id=xxx     - Show diff between local and remote
    10→#   status            - Show sync status of all workflows
    11→#   clean             - Remove local files for workflows deleted from n8n
    12→
    13→set -euo pipefail
    14→
    15→N8N_API_URL="${N8N_API_URL:-http://10.100.5.102:5678/api/v1}"
    16→WORKFLOWS_DIR="${WORKFLOWS_DIR:-$(dirname "$0")/../tofu/apps/n8n/workflows}"
    17→
    18→# Get API key from 1Password
    19→get_api_key() {
    20→    op read "op://homelab/n8n/security/claude_token"
    21→}
    22→
    23→# List all workflows
    24→cmd_list() {
    25→    local api_key
    26→    api_key=$(get_api_key)
    27→
    28→    echo "=== n8n Workflows ==="
    29→    echo ""
    30→    curl -s -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: $api_key" "$N8N_API_URL/workflows" | \
    31→        jq -r '.data[] | "[\(.id)] \(.name) (active: \(.active))"'
    32→}
    33→
    34→# Pull workflows from n8n
    35→cmd_pull() {
    36→    local id="${1:-}"
    37→    local api_key
    38→    api_key=$(get_api_key)
    39→
    40→    mkdir -p "$WORKFLOWS_DIR"
    41→
    42→    if [[ -n "$id" ]]; then
    43→        echo "Pulling workflow $id..."
    44→        local workflow
    45→        workflow=$(curl -s -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: $api_key" "$N8N_API_URL/workflows/$id")
    46→
    47→        if echo "$workflow" | jq -e '.id' > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    48→            local name
    49→            name=$(echo "$workflow" | jq -r '.name' | tr ' ' '_' | tr -cd '[:alnum:]_-')
    50→            local filename="$WORKFLOWS_DIR/${id}_${name}.json"
    51→            echo "$workflow" | jq '.' > "$filename"
    52→            echo "Saved: $filename"
    53→        else
    54→            echo "Error: Workflow $id not found"
    55→            exit 1
    56→        fi
    57→    else
    58→        echo "Pulling all workflows from n8n..."
    59→        local workflows
    60→        workflows=$(curl -s -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: $api_key" "$N8N_API_URL/workflows")
    61→
    62→        echo "$workflows" | jq -r '.data[] | .id' | while read -r wf_id; do
    63→            local workflow
    64→            workflow=$(curl -s -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: $api_key" "$N8N_API_URL/workflows/$wf_id")
    65→            local name
    66→            name=$(echo "$workflow" | jq -r '.name' | tr ' ' '_' | tr -cd '[:alnum:]_-')
    67→            local filename="$WORKFLOWS_DIR/${wf_id}_${name}.json"
    68→            echo "$workflow" | jq '.' > "$filename"
    69→            echo "Saved: $filename"
    70→        done
    71→
    72→        echo ""
    73→        echo "All workflows saved to $WORKFLOWS_DIR"
    74→    fi
    75→}
    76→
    77→# Push workflows to n8n
    78→cmd_push() {
    79→    local id="${1:-}"
    80→    local api_key
    81→    api_key=$(get_api_key)
    82→
    83→    if [[ -n "$id" ]]; then
    84→        local file
    85→        file=$(ls "$WORKFLOWS_DIR/${id}"_*.json 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
    86→        if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
    87→            echo "Error: No local file found for workflow $id"
    88→            exit 1
    89→        fi
    90→
    91→        echo "Pushing workflow from $file..."
    92→        # Only include valid settings fields per n8n API schema
    93→        local payload
    94→        payload=$(jq '{
    95→            name,
    96→            nodes,
    97→            connections,
    98→            settings: {
    99→                saveExecutionProgress: .settings.saveExecutionProgress,
   100→                saveManualExecutions: .settings.saveManualExecutions,
   101→                saveDataErrorExecution: .settings.saveDataErrorExecution,
   102→                saveDataSuccessExecution: .settings.saveDataSuccessExecution,
   103→                executionTimeout: .settings.executionTimeout,
   104→                errorWorkflow: .settings.errorWorkflow,
   105→                timezone: .settings.timezone,
